Kalsang Lhamo traces a series of vertical strokes, slow but firm, practicing Tibetan calligraphy. A 73-year-old retired nurse, she has spoken Tibetan all her life but never learned to write it. Now, in classes at a center for older adults, she immerses herself in the script.

Lhamo also speaks and writes Chinese, which China mandated as its primary language for schools and government agencies in a sweeping new “ethnic unity” law implemented July 1. Under the new regulations, acts deemed to incite division among China’s 56 ethnic groups are prohibited, and schools, families and other institutions are expected to foster patriotism, national unity and a strong sense of community for the Chinese nation.

The law has been widely criticized as a way to further erode the rights of Tibetans and other minorities, and for the authority it gives Beijing to target activities it considers separatist, even outside China. The Chinese government has dismissed foreign criticism as “ideological bias.”

In Tibet — a remote Himalayan region officially designated autonomous but tightly controlled by Beijing — the stakes are particularly high. This year, China is marking the 75th anniversary of what it calls the “peaceful liberation” of Xizang — the Chinese name for Tibet — an event many Tibetans in exile and other critics regard as an invasion.

Some Tibetan activists say the new law represents more forced cultural assimilation and extended control over ethnic minorities. Rights groups say language policies have already been implemented in other minority regions, including expanded Mandarin education for Uyghurs in Xinjiang and the replacement of some Mongolian-language instruction with Mandarin in Inner Mongolia.

“Minority communities that seek to maintain their culture will be pushed toward a double life of public conformity and private reservations,” wrote James Leibold from La Trobe University and Tenzin Dorjee from the advocacy group Tibet Action Institute in Foreign Affairs magazine.

The Associated Press last month joined a government-organized trip to Tibet, including stops in the regional capital, Lhasa, and the city of Shannan, where authorities arranged visits to palaces, Buddhist temples, tourist sites, local businesses and the eldercare center where Lhamo studies. Government officials accompanied the foreign journalists throughout the visit, and AP journalists were not free to move around or conduct reporting independently. The AP retained full editorial control of its content.

Reminders that Tibet is part of China are everywhere, from Chinese airport welcome messages and billboards promoting ethnic unity to Chinese national flags and President Xi Jinping portraits in public squares and buildings.

Some Tibetans, like Lhamo, have found ways to embrace their language and identity, even as critics say the new law pushes China's majority Han culture. In Tibet, that can mean studying the Tibetan script, speaking it at home and with family members, preserving traditional weaving and attending Buddhist rituals.

At these religious sites in Tibet, no signs or references to the Dalai Lama

At the Jokhang Temple, one of Tibet’s holiest religious sites, Tibetans and Han Chinese visited. Some rested outside. Most people in Tibet practice Tibetan Buddhism.

“As a Tibetan, I think it’s important to preserve our language and our culture,” said Qongqiu Quco, a 19-year-old student who came with her aunts, some of them Buddhist nuns.

“Everyone in our ethnic group hopes that our culture can be passed down to future generations,” said Quco, an aspiring teacher who speaks Tibetan much of the time. But at school, she noted, students speak different Tibetan dialects, so they use Mandarin.

For Tibetan Buddhists, the Dalai Lama is their spiritual leader. But at Jokhang Temple, there are no signs or references to the current Dalai Lama, who has lived in exile since fleeing to India after a failed 1959 uprising against Chinese rule.

The succession of the 14th Dalai Lama, who established a government-in-exile unrecognized by Beijing, has become one of the most contentious issues surrounding Tibet. The Dalai Lama has said his successor could be born outside China and that only his office has the authority to recognize his reincarnation.

Beijing says the selection must comply with Chinese law and receive government approval. China has long accused the Dalai Lama of promoting separatism.

The Potala Palace, one of Tibet's most revered sites and once the winter residence of the Dalai Lamas, also had no public reference to the current leader. Thousands visit daily — tourists from across China and local Buddhist believers who pray and leave offerings, including money.

Today, the Chinese national flag flies there.

China's unity law ‘codifies’ policy that's already playing out, an expert says

Benno Weiner, a professor and historian on modern China and Tibet at Carnegie Mellon University in Pittsburgh, said many effects of the policy shift have already been visible for years — particularly stripped-away education and language rights.

“I don’t think the law itself changes things,” he said. “I think it sort of codifies and sort of summarizes a trend that’s been going on.”

Beijing says the policies improve educational opportunities and ensure equal access for ethnic minorities.

The same week as AP's government-organized trip, China’s No. 4-ranked Communist Party leader, Wang Huning, toured Tibet, where he said the priority in governing the region was maintaining stability. He called for the implementation of the unity law and urged authorities to “guide Tibetan Buddhism to adapt to socialist society,” according to a report by state news agency Xinhua.

On its trip, AP visited a traditional Tibetan medicine facility; artisan workshops and cultural centers with traditional crafts, including ceramic making and textile weaving; and a Tibetan opera performance, where workers and performers spoke about the importance of preserving local traditions.

Weiner noted that the Chinese government’s approach to cultural preservation often emphasizes elements seen as less politically sensitive and suitable for tourism.

“The parts of culture that they want to protect and maybe even enhance are the sort of anodyne or nondangerous clothing, certain celebrations that are not religious in many cases,” he said. “Things that maybe not that coincidentally also attract tourists.”

At the Tibet Museum, an exhibit highlights Tibet’s historical links with Chinese dynasties over centuries, a narrative Beijing uses to argue that Tibet has long been part of China. Many Tibetans in exile dispute that, arguing that Tibet was independent for much of its history.

Laba Ciren, the Communist Party's official in charge of the museum, spoke to journalists about the new law. “It only brings benefits and does not have any negative effects,” he said.

Billboards carry the law's message: Promote integration

Access to Tibet is tightly restricted for foreigners. But for those who do arrive, a first observation — after the thinner air, with Lhasa Gonggar International Airport at 3,600 meters (11,800 feet) elevation — might be the official welcome messages.

Some signs are written in Chinese and Tibetan. But outside the terminal, a large sign, in Chinese, says simply: “Xizang welcomes you.”

From highways to city streets in Lhasa and Shannan, billboards promoting ethnic unity are a constant presence. In part, one reads, in Mandarin and then Tibetan: “Forge a strong sense of community for the Chinese nation.”

In Lhasa, Lhamo retired 22 years ago. With her children grown, she tries to make it to classes at the center every day — writing, grammar, poetry — in part because she wasn't able to attend school as a child.

“Our mother tongue is the Tibetan language,” she said proudly.

___

Associated Press video producer Olivia Zhang contributed.

The Pac-12 and Mountain West conferences have finalized a settlement over “poaching” and exit fees.

The two conferences announced on Tuesday that all sides have reached final agreements to settle all pending litigation. The statement included Boise State, Colorado State, Utah State and The Board of Trustees of the California State University on behalf of San Diego State and Fresno State.

“With these matters concluded, the conferences and institutions can move forward with certainty and focus on serving their student-athletes, campuses, fans, and communities,” the statement said.

The conferences announced an agreement in principle in May.

The Pac-12 and some of new the schools joining the conference filed a lawsuit in California in 2024, claiming the poaching clause the league agreed to when it signed a scheduling agreement for its football teams was invalid. The clause called for payments to the Mountain West of $10 million for the first team that left, with the amount increasing by $500,000 for every additional team — to a total of $55 million.

The scheduling agreement with the Mountain West allowed Oregon State and Washington State to piece together football schedules after 10 schools left the Pac-12 in 2024, leaving the conference’s future in doubt.

The Pac-12 had its motion to dismiss denied by Judge Claudia Wilken in November after the sides failed to reach an agreement in mediation last summer.

Colorado State and Utah State filed a separate lawsuit — later joined by Boise State — against the Mountain West seeking to avoid exit fees ranging from $19 million to $38 million.

Colorado State, Utah State, San Diego State, Fresno State and Boise State are set to leave the Mountain West and join the Pac-12 this fall. The conference added Texas State last year to reach the eight-team minimum to be eligible for an automatic bid for its champion in the College Football Playoff.

Gonzaga also is leaving the West Coast Conference to join the Pac-12 as a non-football member this fall.

The Mountain West has added UTEP, Hawaii and Northern Illinois for football starting this fall.

Hours before President Donald Trump’s visit to his Rancho Palos Verdes golf club, Los Angeles County sheriff’s investigators announced Tuesday that a man had been arrested over the weekend after allegedly taking photos and videos at the property while “appearing to monitor security-planning activities.”

Authorities said Jeanine John Taele, 38, of Downey, was arrested Sunday after deputies found hollow-point ammunition in his pocket and a loaded firearm inside his vehicle, which was parked at Trump National Golf Club. A subsequent search of his home uncovered additional firearms, body armor, high-capacity magazines and multiple notebooks containing what investigators described as “concerning statements,” officials said.

Officials did not disclose the contents of the notebooks.

Trump is scheduled to speak Tuesday evening at a Republican National Committee fundraiser at the golf club.

Trump is scheduled to speak Tuesday evening at a Republican National Committee fundraiser at the golf club ( Chip Somodevilla/Getty Images )

Taele was being held without bail, according to county jail records.

According to the District Attorney's Office, Taele was charged Tuesday with manufacturing, importing, keeping for sale, giving or receiving a large-capacity magazine; possession of a short-barreled rifle or shotgun; and a count of second-degree robbery that allegedly occurred in November 2025, all felonies. He was also charged with a misdemeanor count of carrying a concealed firearm in a vehicle.

He was scheduled to appear in a Torrance courtroom Tuesday afternoon for arraignment. There was no immediate word on whether that hearing had been held.

According to the sheriff's department, deputies were called to the Trump National Golf Club in Rancho Palos Verdes around 3:30 p.m. Sunday by federal agents who spotted a "suspicious individual" on the property.

"The individual was observed walking throughout the golf course grounds taking photographs and videos and appearing to monitor security- planning activities," sheriff's officials said in a statement.

Deputies detained Taele and discovered he was being investigated by police in El Segundo on suspicion of robbery. While detaining Taele, deputies found a 16-round magazine containing hollow-point ammunition in a pants pocket. Deputies also searched his vehicle and found "a loaded pistol with a round chambered, along with an additional loaded magazine containing hollow point ammunition," according to the sheriff's department.

Sheriff's detectives assigned to the FBI's Joint Terrorism Task Force served a warrant Monday at Taele's home. According to the sheriff's department, investigators found:

an illegally modified AR platform rifle

a 1911 .45-caliber pistol

an AR platform upper receiver

body armor

high-capacity magazines

bulk pistol and rifle ammunition

multiple notebooks containing "concerning statements"

two radio signal devices

It was unclear if the "concerning statements" included any threats of violence toward Trump.

"Currently, investigators have identified no credible threat to our communities," according to a sheriff's department statement. "However, this case underscores the importance of vigilance, strong partnerships with local, state, and federal law enforcement agencies, and the proactive steps taken to identify and investigate suspicious activity before it can escalate."

Trump is expected to be the headline speaker at an RNC dinner at the Rancho Palos Verdes golf club Tuesday night. According to the White House, he is expected to make remarks on his administration's economic policies and successes in reducing crime. He is also expected to level criticism at Democratic California Gov. Gavin Newsom, a potential presidential candidate.

News.title: Rep. Max Miller uses CNN interview to drag Trump, Hegseth and his 2-year-old daughter into ‘abuse’ battle with ex-wife
News.content:

Rep. Max Miller publicly took the first questions from a reporter regarding the shocking claims made by his ex-wife in an ongoing court battle on Tuesday as he sat down for an interview with CNN’s Jake Tapper.

Miller is accused by his ex-wife of scalding her with hot water and physically abusing both her and their daughter, whom Miller’s ex-wife claims had her collarbone broken by the Ohio Republican congressman. Those claims, which he denied in a video message on Sunday morning, were first revealed publicly by Mother Jones, detailing court documents filed in a defamation case Miller is pursuing against his ex-wife. Her father, U.S. Sen. Bernie Moreno, echoed those accusations and told reporters on the Hill this week that his daughter lives in fear of Miller and what he might do.

The interview Tuesday was tense, though Miller never lost his temper, as Tapper repeatedly pressed him about heartwrenching statements his daughter was alleged to have made about him and the home where she stays with him temporarily as part of a shared custody agreement.

At one point, the anchor questioned whether he was being inconsistent in his own characterization of his daughter’s verbal abilities.

“There is a police report from the suspected child abuse incident in February involving your daughter, and that report details that the child protection team says that your child had a right clavicle fracture, and “a bruise that accompanies the injury that appears to be in a handprint and appears to have been inflicted,” Tapper told Miller.

open image in gallery Rep. Max Miller denied accusations of abusing his ex-wife, daughter, and former girlfriends on CNN ( CNN - The Lead with Jake Tapper )

”Your ex-wife stated to police that your child told her in the days leading up to the discovery of the injury, quote daddy kill you, and your ex-wife also said your child had said, ' Daddy angry and daddy's house is scary,” he continued.

“Jake, I wish you could talk to my beautiful baby girl. She can't string together sentences like that. She's two and a half years old,” the congressman responded.

Tapper then shot back: “You just told me that she had said that she was scared to go to mommy's house.”

“She is. I have video of it,” said Miller.

open image in gallery Rep. Max Miller is up for re-election in a district that leans Republican in just three months ( Getty )

open image in gallery Sen. Bernie Moreno, his former father-in-law, urged Miller to quit Congress and seek psychological help ( Reuters )

“But now you're saying that she's not capable of saying ‘Daddy kill you?’” asked Tapper. “I mean, it seems like she's either able to say one but not the other. That doesn't make sense.”

Miller responded: “Jake. To be very direct, this is incredibly disturbing...You have to look at the timing of everything that is taking place, right? What about due process?”

Miller would repeatedly insist throughout the interview that he’d been investigated for the claims made by his ex-wife, and found to be innocent. He had no explanation for why his ex-girlfriend Stephanie Grisham, a former Trump White House aide, was also accusing him of abusive behavior, though he denied them as well.

And Miller invoked the allegations of lewd and unconsensual sexual behavior leveled at Donald Trump during the 2016 election cycle as he vowed to stay in his race for re-election.

“There are now three women who have accused you of violent behavior. Are all three of these women who don't know each other lying?” asked Tapper.

“Yes,” said Miller. “In 2016, when Donald J. Trump faced the most extreme allegations in the world that hit him day after day after day...guess what? He stayed in and he was resilient.”

At another point in the interview, he turned to Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth as he explained why the Daily Mail had obtained pictures showing syringes found in his bedroom. During recorded conversations with his ex-wife Miller released as part of a trove of documents related to his divorce proceedings over the weekend, his ex-wife can be heard accusing him of having a “drug problem”.

“This is testosterone replacement therapy. People are painting this as something that it’s not. Secretary Hegseth, who is the Secretary of War, just three weeks ago, allowed our entire military, who are males, to take testosterone replacement therapy. That's what I was doing. I have not been using any illegal drugs. This is nonsense.”

Miller is running for his third House term in a relatively safe Republican district in Ohio, but the nature of the allegations has some Republicans fearing his chances of holding the seat.

One of those Republicans is Trump himself. Now facing the first midterm cycle of his second term, the president is staring down the likely possibility of his party losing one or possibly even both of their twin congressional majorities to the Democrats in the fall. Miller’s shaky candidacy could make the Democrats’ path to taking the House an easier prospect.

Trump reportedly called Miller on Monday to express his doubts about the congressman’s candidacy, but Miller said Tuesday that he would remain in the race.

Complicating the matter for him is his former father-in-law, Sen. Bernie Moreno, a fellow Republican, who spoke to reporters this week about how his daughter Emily lives in “constant fear” of the congressman, and has urged him to drop out of Congress.

“This is truly the seventh level of hell,” Moreno told reporters on Monday. “This has been a horrific experience for my entire family.”

“My daughter lives in constant fear of this man, not like something that’s existential, but deeply in her heart, she fears what this guy is capable of,” he continued.

The Justice Department knew or should have known for weeks that its case against a former Olympian charged with intentionally damaging the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool was flawed, and that he bore no responsibility for longstanding problems at the landmark, defense lawyers said Tuesday.

U.S. Attorney Jeanine Pirro on Friday moved to dismiss the indictment against David Hearn, saying in a 20-page filing that newly produced evidence from the Interior Department showed the former Olympic canoeist was not responsible for damage to the pool's lining.

Pirro’s office attributed the damage instead to a botched installation by a contractor as well as “the rush to complete the project prior to events associated with the America 250 celebration” in the weeks surrounding July 4, as directed by President Donald Trump.

Lawyers for Hearn urged a judge to permanently dismiss the case and foreclose the possibility that the Trump administration could revive it. They took issue with Pirro's assertion that prosecutors only recently learned about the flawed contracting work.

“From the outset, the evidence showed that the pool liner was already failing and that Mr. Hearn did not cause the damage alleged in the indictment,'' Hearn's legal team argued in a 28-page motion filed Tuesday in D.C. Superior Court.

The poor condition of the pool was “plainly visible” for weeks and was publicly documented through photographs, video and news reports, lawyers Mary Dohrmann, Steve Levin and Norman Eisen wrote.

The contractor, Virginia-based Atlantic Industrial Coatings, “publicly acknowledged, before Mr. Hearn was indicted, that portions of the project required repair,” the lawyers said. The firm was awarded a $14.7 million no-bid contract to repaint and waterproof the pool's concrete floor.

Trump said Monday that Pirro “choked” and “folded like an umbrella” in moving to drop charges against Hearn. Trump, who met with Pirro late Monday, said he remained disappointed by her assessment that damage to the Reflecting Pool was the result of shoddy construction, not vandalism.

The dismissal of charges against Hearn was an embarrassing setback for the Justice Department and marked a rare moment during Trump’s second term of an aide or political appointee openly defying him.

Hearn has said he was on a bike ride June 19 when he reached in to examine the pool’s newly peeled coating and briefly touched a chunk attached to the side of the pool. But he said he obeyed a park worker who told him to let go of it.

Felony charges, including a possible prison sentence, were brought “without a meaningful investigation into the central and obvious question in this case: whether Mr. Hearn caused, or even could have caused, any damage to the Reflecting Pool,'' Hearn's lawyers said. “Defying both decency and common sense, the government proceeded to indict Mr. Hearn before it had obtained or evaluated the information necessary to establish a good-faith basis for the charge.”

News.title: Spokane fire suspect served time for manslaughter before arson arrest
News.content:
Aaron F. Farinacci, 37, was arrested and charged with first-degree arson for allegedly setting the Old Trails Fire, the largest of three wildfires that have caused widespread destruction in and around Spokane, Washington.

The fires have destroyed at least 700 buildings and forced the evacuation of approximately 67,000 people, with the blazes remaining uncontained as of Tuesday morning.

Farinacci's arrest in the investigation into the fires stemmed from a community tip. He was found to have matches and a lighter on him and had previously served prison time for manslaughter in Arizona.

In 2010, Farinacci, then age 21, shot and killed his father during an argument about washing dishes, police said at the time. Farinacci also shot himself but survived. He was charged with murder but pleaded guilty in 2012 to manslaughter and aggravated assault, records show. Farinacci was released from prison in 2020.

Firefighting efforts are ongoing with over 1,000 personnel, though conditions were expected to deteriorate due to anticipated high winds and temperatures, further challenging containment. Many residents have returned to find their homes completely incinerated, and while no deaths or major injuries have been reported, an expedited emergency declaration was approved to aid the affected areas.

A South Florida steakhouse is turning heads with a cheeky way to spice up date night: a nude five-course dining experience.

C.L.A.S.S. Soiree Steakhouse in Hollywood hosts the clothing-optional event on the first Monday each month, drawing attention on social media and around town for its unusual dress code - or lack thereof.

The dinners typically attract about 20 guests, with tickets priced at $250 for men, $150 for women and $300 for couples, Local 10 reports. Guests begin removing their clothing once they enter the restaurant, with private areas available for changing.

When asked by the outlet Monday whether having nude guests could be distracting, chef and owner Maurad Ali pushed back, saying, “I’m the chef and owner; my crew, we are all professionals,” emphasizing that the event is focused on dining and socializing, not anything inappropriate.

The restaurant also has rules in place to keep the event private. Employees must remain fully clothed, and windows are covered so people outside cannot see in, which helped city officials confirm the event is legal, Local 10 News reports.

open image in gallery C.L.A.S.S. Soiree Steakhouse in Hollywood, Florida, hosts a naked dining experience on the first Monday of each month, typically with 20 guests ( Google Maps )

open image in gallery Tickets for the event are priced at $250 for men, $150 for women and $300 for couples ( AFP/Getty )

Ali said he created the nude concept to attract new customers and generate buzz, saying there is demand for the experience.

“It's more so a gathering - to get to know people, new people in the city, in the lifestyle,” hostess Tashaeba Hart added.

While some guests were eager to dig in, others weren’t ready to take a bite out of the idea.

“Finally a place where I don’t have to plan what to wear,” one person joked on an Instagram post shared by the restaurant and Local 10 News.

Another commenter served up a pun of their own, writing, “I hope the naked dining is ‘Well Done.’”

But some critics had beef with the idea, questioning whether it fit the restaurant’s reputation.

“Bro. Whyyyy? Part of what we loved so much about CLASS was that it was classy,” one commenter wrote.

Another added, “Yea I’ll pass, wouldn’t go there even if it was free….”

News.title: What I saw in a week on the front line of Afghanistan’s hunger crisis
News.content:
May 15 and 16, 2026

It is the weekend, a small moment to rest, although there is still a lot of work waiting for me. A week in the field does not mean that work in Kabul stops. I try to catch up on my emails and have a planned online interview for an international staff position – since in Europe, Friday is a normal working day. I also review parts of new proposals for donors and our financial planning.

On Saturday, however, I take a short break. Together with the base management team in Helmand, we visit a historical site called Qala-e-Bost, believed to have been built around 3,000 years ago. It is a rare moment to step away from work, followed by lunch with the team.

May 17, 2026

Sunday morning, the first working day of the week, we visit Basrhan Sub Health Centre, run by one of our local partners. As a nurse and former nurse trainer, I feel very much in my element in these health centres. It allows me to engage easily with the team and discuss their work.

I speak with the outreach officer and the vaccinator. They explain that this facility supports 18 outreach locations, each visited at least once a month. They provide vaccinations, raise awareness, and connect communities to the health centre. These visits often take place in simple settings, like mosques.

Immunisation is now well accepted. In the beginning, there was some resistance, but trust has grown over time. Every child is tracked, and if a child misses a vaccination, community health volunteers follow up at home. For extra polio vaccinations, this is carefully recorded by marking a finger of the child – helping ensure that no child is missed. The goal is clear: a polio-free Afghanistan.

I also speak with a mother. She is wearing a burka, so I cannot see her face. She tells me she is 22 years old and holds her 12-month-old son on her lap. She came because he has a fever, but I see a healthy child – something that stands out after my time in the TFU.

She brings her child regularly for follow-up and growth monitoring and the child has never been in a treatment program for malnutrition. She speaks positively about the services. “We are lucky,” she says. “The staff treat us well, and we have access to care in our community.”

News.title: World’s first seahorse hospital fights to protect them from extinction
News.content:
With careful precision, marine biologist Linda Albonetti extracts a 10cm-long injured seahorse – a heavily pregnant male – from an aquarium tank to apply healing ointment to its wound.

Linda, 29, coordinator at the world’s first specialist seahorse hospital, is currently caring for around 50 of these tiny creatures, all of which were brought in by local fishing crews after becoming snagged in their nets.

The seahorse will be kept for a few more days before it is released back into the Adriatic Sea, giving it time to recover from the cut to the soft, bony plates that form its outer carapace.

What the team here are doing is a literal drop in the ocean, a small attempt to fight back against the potential extinction of these remarkable fish.

In Europe and around countries like Indonesia, they are being poached in their millions for sale to a voracious Asian traditional medicine market where they are consumed as an aphrodisiac and alleged cure for impotence, asthma and kidney problems.

“There is definitely a downward trend in the overall seahorse population because they are being collected for the Asian market,” says Linda. “Technically, they cannot be exported to countries such as China, but there is no specific law preventing that trade. They do not have the same protections as sea turtles, for example.

“It is not happening in this part of Italy yet, but it is further south, off the Mediterranean coast. That is why it is so important that we monitor their numbers and maintain a good relationship with the local fishermen.”

News.title: The 13 best castle hotels in England
News.content:
Few places capture the imagination quite like a castle, and England is home to some of the most remarkable places to spend the night. If it’s not the romance of waking up in a canopied four-poster bed, or losing ourselves in centuries-old tapestries and visceral oil paintings, we are lured by tales of brave knights and plotting dignitaries, duplicitous royals and ghosts parleying secrets in the hallways.

Part of the magic is spending an afternoon wandering grounds and gardens followed by evenings in front of a roaring fire, or dining in a banquet hall that may have hosted medieval kings and queens. While not every castle has crenellated battlements, glistening moats or royal connections, each stony stronghold on our list has something special that makes it worth travelling for. In this modern age that might include a spa, fine-dining restaurant or extra touches like free admission to exhibitions and museum tours. Here’s our pick of the best castle hotels in England.

News.title: Careless Liverpool concede same goal twice in second-half capitulation against Leeds
News.content:
Soldier Field in Chicago hosts an all-Premier League tie encounter as Liverpool take on Leeds as both sides bring their US tours to a close. Both Premier League encounters between these sides last season ended in draws; a 3-3 draw at Elland Road was followed up by a 0-0 stalemate at Anfield. The draw at Elland Road was immediately followed by Mohamed Salah speaking to the media, claiming he had been thrown under the bus.

It is a new era at Liverpool as former Bournemouth boss Andoni Iraola has replaced Arne Slot at Anfield. They kicked off the Iraola era in Nashville, Tennessee, with a 4-2 win over Sunderland, following that up with another victory in New York on Wednesday night, beating Wrexham 1-0, and will be aiming to make it three wins from three on their US tour.

“I think it [the US tour] has been really, really useful,” Iraola said in an interview on the official Liverpool website. Obviously, you spend a lot of time with the players, with the staff, you get all the information you can. And I think there is also an evolution, it has to be. We start to understand each other better, what we need to do. Every game, I hope we can get closer and closer and put ourselves in a position where the few players that still are not here start to train also, they are helped by the others.”

Virgil van Dijk and Cody Gakpo resumed training back on Merseyside whilst Alexis Mac Allister, Alisson and Victor Munoz are yet to return to training following their World Cup exploits. The trio of Florian Wirtz, Alexander Isak and Ryan Gravenberch are all set to feature for the first time this pre-season.

Leeds’ pre-season campaign began with a 3-2 loss to Championship Wrexham in Tampa, Florida before beating Sunderland 1-0 in New Jersey courtesy of a long-range strike from Lukas Nmecha. Former Liverpool man Harry Wilson joined Leeds on a free from Fulham this summer.

“Really tough but that is expected,” Wilson said. That is what pre-season is for, building up a base for when the season starts, making sure you are in the best physical position you can be to attack the season. It has been good. I played against them [Leeds] twice last year when I was at Fulham. Both games were really, really tough games.

“I think when the fans have got a good team to support, I think that [the atmosphere at Elland Road] goes up a notch. I think the size of the club was a massive part of me coming. Then speaking to the guys, the chairman, the sporting director, and seeing kind of the plans and the aims for the club, it is something I wanted to be a part of.”

Team news to follow shortly.

News.title: Oil plummets as Trump calls off Iran strikes
News.content:
Oil prices have plunged after Donald Trump called off strikes and said the US and Iran would hold further peace talks.

Brent crude, the international benchmark, sank as much as 9.5pc early on Monday to less than $82 a barrel after the US president said he had halted plans for “disastrous” strikes.

Mr Trump said: “Obviously, they don’t want to be attacked. They knew the extent of the attack because they saw it forming.

“Now what we’re doing is we’re talking to them in the form of a negotiation. It begins tomorrow afternoon.”

Mr ‌Trump also ordered oil companies to lower petrol prices for American ‌consumers ‌and criticised ⁠Chevron’s chief executive for not crediting his administration for supporting the fossil fuel industry.

The president said that he had been asked by Iran as well as US partners Saudi Arabia, the United Arab Emirates and Qatar to hold off on strikes. He halted plans for a major attack against Iran on Saturday, which he said would have been the biggest since the Second World War.

Mr Trump claimed the sides were on the “perimeter” of a peace deal.

Oil’s sharp fall also sent the cost of government borrowing lower on Monday over hopes that it would ease inflation.

The yield on 10-year UK gilts, a benchmark for what the Treasury pays to borrow money, dropped from 5.05pc to 4.98pc, while the equivalent US bonds dropped from 4.74pc to 4.69pc.

Stock markets in Europe also rose, with the FTSE 100 up 0.2pc, the Cac 40 in Paris up 0.3pc and the Dax in Frankfurt climbing 0.1pc.

News.title: Inside the trial for a vaccine to end malaria
News.content:
A small group of brave volunteers were given an experimental vaccine in Oxford this week in a bid to bring to an end the centuries-old scourge of malaria.

“I’m on my second vaccine now. Then I’m due to have my third vaccine soon, and then in November, I’ll be given malaria,” said an upbeat Mike Luciw, a 32-year-old local who works in recruitment.

“The hope is to help find something that could save millions of people.”

There are already two licenced vaccines for malaria but the new Oxford “RH5” shot is not like anything that has come before.

The existing jabs only act against malaria as it moves towards the liver in the early stage of infection, and provide only partial protection.

The new combination vaccine, in contrast, is designed to fight it off both at the liver stage and in the wider bloodstream, effectively knocking it out altogether.

The project is being run by the husband and wife team of Simon Draper, Professor of Vaccinology and Translational Medicine at the University of Oxford, and Professor Angela Minassian, an infectious disease specialist and clinical lead for their malaria programme in Oxford’s Department of Paediatrics.

“The dream for malaria … has been to have these two lines of defence, liver and blood, so if the first line fails, you’ve got a second,” says Prof Draper, who leads on the science.

“Our dream is to have a vaccine that gives over 90 per cent efficacy in African children,” adds Prof Minassian, who heads the clinical trials for the new jab.

News.title: Dowman weaves his magic and new signing shines as Arsenal hit ground running
News.content:
Hello and welcome to our live coverage for this pre-season friendly between Girona and Arsenal at Estadi Montilivi in Catalonia.

With the transfer speculation surrounding Vinícius Júnior’s and Bruno Guimaraes’ potential moves to Arsenal ramping up, the reigning Premier League champions are in action against Girona as they step up their preparations ahead of the upcoming campaign.

Unlike other Premier League heavyweights, Arsenal have kept their pre-season tour relatively local with a selection of games in Spain, Ireland and England, before they face Manchester City in the FA Community Shield on August 16 at the Millennium Stadium in Cardiff.

Arsenal beat League One side MK Dons 3-0 in a behind-closed-doors friendly on July 25 at the Sobha Realty Training Centre, thanks to goals from Reiss Nelson, Ethan Nwaneri and Ceadach O’Neill.

After featuring in this victory and setting up Nelson for the opener, Christos Tzolis will be looking to continue his positive momentum with his new club, after joining Arsenal for £34m earlier this summer. Many fans will be keeping a close eye on the recently-signed winger given that various core members of last season’s Premier League-winning squad are yet to return from their post-World Cup breaks, having progressed deep in the competition.

Tournament winners David Raya, Martin Zubimendi and Mikel Merino, Norway captain Martin Odegaard, as well as England internationals Bukayo Saka, Declan Rice, Eberechi Eze and Noni Madueke are all missing for this game, while France’s William Saliba is out injured and set for an extended period on the sidelines.

Those who exited the World Cup earlier than the aforementioned players, including Gabriel Magalhaes, Gabriel Martinelli, Piero Hincapie, Kai Havertz, and Viktor Gyokeres, have all joined up with the squad in northern Spain.

Mikel Arteta’s men will play a wounded Girona, who suffered relegation from the top flight of Spanish football last season due to a 19th-place finish.

Kick-off is at 19:00, with team news arriving shortly.

News.title: Josh Kerr turns ‘race of the century’ into one-sided show of power
News.content:
For many the 100m is the Blue Riband event the one everyone wants to watch and the race that steals all the headlines. For these Commonwealth Games, however, tonight’s mile race is the one that has grabbed all the attention – and it is not hard to see why.

Josh Kerr, fresh from his new world record of 3:42.66 (a time that beat a mark that had stood since 1999) takes on fellow Scot Jake Wightman and Australia’s new superstar Cameron Myers. Three great runners over a distance that evokes sepia-tinted memories of Roger Bannister and the seminal four-minute mark.

Some of you may be wondering why the mile is back at an international event. Well, Seb Coe, the president of World Athletics and someone who broke the mile record three times, says the race distance is easy to understand and resonates with fans. And, coming on the back of Kerr’s world record, who can argue with him?

This is the first time the mile has been run at the games since 1966 and the hope is that tonight’s final matches the Miracle Mile run in 1954. Earlier that year Bannister broke the four-minute barrier, only for Australia’s John Landy to go lower with a time of 3:58.0 soon after. The Games in Vancouver were the first time two sub-four minuters had gone head-to-head. And the race didn’t disappoint – Bannister beating Landy with a time of 3:58.8 minutes. The Australian also ran under four minutes, making it the first time two men had done so in the same race.

Obviously all three of the expected main protagonists will go well under four minutes, but if they can recreate the drama of the 1954 final then we’ll have a race to savour.

Stay here for all the action with the gun set to go off at 8.55.

Sports.title: Man Utd share 1,698-word statement over controversial ticket tout crackdown after 1 device accessed over 1,000 accounts
Sports.content:
MANCHESTER UNITED say ONE device gained access to 1,088 membership accounts to fuel a ticket touting operation.

United have been pilloried by fans after thousands were locked out of their accounts amid apparent suspicious activity.



The club restricted accounts where login details were shared with more than six people in a bid to clamp down on touting.

SunSport revealed the most skilled touts had not been affected as they used innovative methods to bypass settings.



Fan groups were scathing in their assessment of the process.

And the Manchester United Supporters’ Trust was “inundated” with complaints from supporters affected.



That prompted a 1,698-word update on the club website.

The Red Devils acknowledged its approach had caused “genuine upset and distress”.

United did not offer an apology.

But they vowed to share findings once their investigation was over and thanked fans for their “feedback and challenge”.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

The club said: “Our intention is to protect fair access to tickets for genuine United supporters and to tackle organised ticket touting and abuse of the ticketing system.”

Meanwhile, Red Devils have given boss Michael Carrick a boost by striking a record £20million training kit deal with gambling firm Betway — the largest in world football.

And United are set to name ex-Hearts chief Eva Olid as women’s manager.

Sports.title: Beleaguered Fifa boss Infantino holed up in desperate crisis talks to cling to power as Wenger joins blackmail rebellion
Sports.content:
GIANNI INFANTINO has called an emergency crisis Fifa meeting in a desperate attempt to cling on to his power.

And now Arsene Wenger has joined the growing group distancing themselves from the Swiss chief.



Infantino, 56, sparked chaos around world football last week when news broke of his shock plans to sell off stakes in the World Cup.

That sparked a furious backlash from swathes of football – including Uefa and other continental confederations, who threatened to boycot the World Cup and even plotted to launch a rival tournament to “paralyse Fifa”.



Under overwhelming and mounting pressure, Infantino was forced to make an embarrassing U-turn and ditch his money-grabbing scheme – and now faces a fight to keep hold of his Fifa presidency.

Now he is taking extreme measures to try and retain any support he can.



According to The Times, Infantino is currently holed up in Rabat and has called senior Fifa staff to the Moroccan capital for the urgent gathering.

There was also said to be a meeting of senior Fifa staff on Tuesday without Infantino present, where all but one opposed the controversial World Cup financial plot.

Even so, the chief’s remaining loyal right-hand men are shamelessly appealing to many of the 211 member associations to publicly back the president, who faces an election in March if he survives that long.

But few have done so – including, crucially, Saudi Arabia, hosts of the 2034 World Cup.



CASINO SPECIAL – BEST CASINO BONUSES FROM £10 DEPOSITS

Jordan FA president Prince Ali bin Al Hussein launched a damning attack on the Swiss and his organisation, making accusations of “blackmail”.

It is even claimed Fifa withheld funds owed to the Jordan FA – and that the Asian national team federation would benefit from backing Infantino.

Prince Ali bin Al Hussein, 50, wrote on X: “There is no shortage of issues regarding Fifa.

“We have been waiting for reward money for our players since December for the Arab Cup in Qatar, which is a Fifa event.



“The money our team should receive for having reached the final has not been delivered yet, while at the same time Fifa brags about how many billions they have in reserve.

“It is clear the problem really is with leadership.

“For months, Fifa has been refusing to help us on any of these or other matters – until it was verbally communicated to me during the World Cup that if I endorsed Infantino it would go a long way to helping our FA out.

“We pride ourselves in Jordan in upholding ethical values.

“We did not endorse him before and certainly will not now.



“But the whole situation amounts to blackmail and we refuse to give in to that.”

Within the top brass at Fifa, both Arsene Wenger and Secretary General Mattias Grafstrom have slammed Infantino’s disgraceful plans.

Wenger admitted it was “absolutely necessary” to scrap the scheme – which included setting up a company called Fifa Forward Enterprises (FFE) with a stake held by Donald Trump’s son-in-law’s brother Joshua Kusher – and that he had no idea about it until it became public knowledge.



Fifa’s head of global football development does not intent to quit and said: “The recent events at Fifa deserve some clarity from my side.

“I was not involved in this strategic plan and first became aware of the project through media reports.

“The decision to withdraw the project was absolutely necessary and beyond question, because I firmly believe in an independent Fifa that serves our game with commitment, transparency and integrity.”

Grafstrom, meanwhile, sent an email to Fifa staff in an attempt to boost morale after “a sad and reproachable series of events”.

Grafstrom said: “We have all been thrown into the middle of a turmoil, which is difficult to comprehend and accept, but, as Secretary General, I urge you to remain focused on what has always united us: serving football and serving our 211 member associations.



“A sad and reproachable series of events — which were thankfully concluded with the FFE project permanently abandoned — for as much as we feel dismayed by them, should not overshadow this reality.

“I assure you that you as members of the administration, you will be defended and safeguarded from the political context we currently experience.

“You do not need to worry.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“Individuals, unstable moments and unfortunate episodes come and go.

“The institution, its mission and its responsibility towards world football continue, and that is why we should always keep our professionalism, sense of perspective and composure.”

Sports.title: Liverpool legend Mo Salah ‘agrees two-year deal with Trabzonspor’ on free as Turkish club release transfer statement
Sports.content:
MOHAMED SALAH has agreed to join Turkish side Trabzonspor on a free transfer.

The Liverpool legend left the Premier League side at the end of the 2025/26 campaign.



Salah, 34, has reportedly agreed to move to the Turkish Super Lig on a two-year contract.

Trabzonspor confirmed that they were in negotiations with the attacker on social media.



The club then revealed that Salah would be arriving in Istanbul on Wednesday ahead of finalising the transfer.

A statement read: “Professional footballer Mohamed Salah, with whom we have begun transfer negotiations, will be at Istanbul Atatürk Airport General Aviation Terminal at 12:00 on Wednesday, August 5 (tomorrow).



“The player is scheduled to arrive in Trabzon on the same day in the evening hours.

“The time and other details regarding the welcome program in Trabzon will be shared with the public through our club’s official communication channels during the day.”

Salah will be familiar with at least one of his new team-mates, with one being former Manchester United goalkeeper Andre Onana.

The stopper spent last season on loan at the club and has returned for a second stint this summer.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

He will also join former Manchester City defender Stefan Savic and Cape Verde’s World Cup star Sidny Lopes Cabral in the squad.

Salah announced he would leave Liverpool back in March after nine years with the club.

He signed for the club in 2017 from Serie A side Roma and went on to become one of its best-ever players.

The forward has scored an astonishing 255 goals in 435 appearances in all competitions.



He helped the Reds to two Premier League titles, the Champions League, Fifa Club World Cup, FA Cup and two EFL Cups.

In the summer, Salah helped Egypt reach the last-16 of the World Cup, which is the furthest ever made by the nation.

He scored one goal and assisted twice in five tournament appearances.

Last season, Trabzonspor finished third in the Super Lig, eight points behind champions Galatasaray.

Sports.title: Rapper Drake called me to convince me to quit Tottenham.. I thought it was Aaron Lennon winding me up says Jermain Defoe
Sports.content:
JERMAIN DEFOE says music icon Drake persuaded him to join Toronto from Tottenham – but only after thinking Aaron Lennon was playing a cruel prank.

The legendary striker, 43, hit the headlines when his spell as Woking’s boss ended after only SIX competitive showdowns last month.



But Defoe, who was blasted by the non-league minnows following his exit, had a stunning career with Spurs.

He made 363 appearances across two spells on Tottenham’s books – notching 143 goals along the way.



Defoe quit the North Londoners when MLS side Toronto came calling in 2014.

And Canadian rapper Drake was tasked with convincing the England icon to make the stunning move.

But Defoe was certain Tottenham team-mate Lennon, 39, was winding him up when he picked up the phone.

The former West Ham and Portsmouth marksman told the Mirror: “I remember being out for dinner with my cousin.

“I got a phone call, said ‘hello, who’s this’, and he said ‘It’s Drake’. Yeah, good one – I thought he was winding me up!

“I actually thought it was Aaron Lennon, I thought, ‘Wow, your Canadian accent is unbelievable’. But no, it was Drake.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

“We had a conversation and I remember he spoke about Toronto, the city, what it’s like, the people, the football club, and that was it. I decided to sign and I loved it.”

Defoe went on to find the net 12 times in 21 appearances for the Canadian side, whose home was on hosting duties for this summer’s World Cup.

And it allowed him to reunite with ex-Tottenham pal Ryan Nelsen, who was in charge of Toronto, despite initially having doubts.

The lethal finisher, who bagged a brace at Soccer Aid in June, added: “I remember getting a call from Ryan Nelsen.



“I played with Ryan at Tottenham towards the back end of his career. Obviously, he got the Toronto job and we spoke about the opportunity of going there.

“At the time I said I don’t think it’s going to happen because I was at Tottenham and I was settled and didn’t really think I was going to leave.”

Defoe reignited his Premier League career by joining Sunderland after a year-long spell with Toronto.

And he returned to the Stadium of Light, following stints with Bournemouth and Rangers, before announcing his retirement in 2022.

Sports.title: Jordan FA chief accuses Gianni Infantino of ‘BLACKMAIL’ in most scathing statement yet: ‘We certainly won’t endorse him’
Sports.content:
GIANNI INFANTINO and Fifa have been accused of “blackmail” in the most scathing statement yet.

The head of world football’s governing body has come under intense criticism since his failed plot to sell off stakes in the World Cup and other Fifa events.



He backed down after a chaotic few days which saw football bodies around the world threaten a rebellion.

But despite the plans being thrown in the bin, Infantino continues to come under heavy fire as he desperately tries to cling on to the Fifa presidency.



However, the president of the Jordan FA launched a damning attack on the Swiss.

And it is even claimed Fifa withheld funds owed to the Jordan FA – and that the Asian national team federation would benefit from backing Infantino.

But the Jordan FA took a strong stance and insist they “refuse to give in” or “endorse” Infantino.

Prince Ali bin Al Hussein, 50, wrote on X: “There is no shortage of issues regarding Fifa.

“Let me start by clarifying what some of these are from an FA perspective, in particular that of Jordan going into a World Cup for the first time.

“We are a small country with a minimal budget for our FA and had to deal with enormous hurdles.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

“First, getting our fans into the USA: not all were granted visas, even though they had tickets – which we also know were sold at exorbitant prices.

“Secondly, we are being taxed by the US govt through Fifa for our participation.

“Money that should go to players and staff.

“This was not the case for those who played and set up camp in Canada and Mexico.



“But we happened to be in the USA so now we face these huge costs in taxes for having participated.

“Thirdly we have been waiting for reward money for our players since December for the Arab Cup in Qatar, which is a Fifa event.

“The money our team should receive for having reached the final has not been delivered yet, while at the same time Fifa brags about how many billions they have in reserve.

“It is clear the problem really is with leadership.

“For months, Fifa has been refusing to help us on any of these or other matters – until it was verbally communicated to me during the World Cup that if I endorsed Infantino it would go a long way to helping our FA out.



“We pride ourselves in Jordan in upholding ethical values.

“We did not endorse him before and certainly will not now.

“But the whole situation amounts to blackmail and we refuse to give in to that.”

SunSport has contacted Fifa for comment in response to Prince Ali’s tweet.

Interestingly, the support of national associations in Asia could be critical to Infantino’s re-election campaign in March.



However, he may not even reach that far if Fifa council members opt to oust him.

Uefa cranked up the pressure on Arsene Wenger to quit as Fifa’s head of global football development – but he has no intention of doing so.

European football chiefs, meanwhile, are ready to team up with other confederations to set up a rival World Cup to “paralyse Fifa”.

Infantino’s furious opponents are also prepared to boycott Fifa council and committee meetings, as well as refuse to ratify decisions.

The shameless lawyer has only notched 15 declarations of support from the 211 member nations since his botched project was revealed.

And The FA joined their Welsh counterparts in withdrawing their backing ahead of next year’s presidential election.

Sports.title: ITV confirm five Championship games to be shown for FREE including Millwall vs West Ham and more monster derbies
Sports.content:
FIERCE rivals Millwall and West Ham are set to lock horns for the first time in 14 years next month – and ITV will be screening the showdown for free.

The Hammers, who sold Freddie Potts to Club Brugge earlier today, are among the favourites to win the Championship title this season.



West Ham are desperate to seal an immediate return to the Premier League after suffering relegation on the final day of last term.

But Millwall are also heading into the new campaign dreaming of bagging a place in the top flight.

Boro, who lost to Hull City in last season’s play-off final, are in line to battle it out with the Baggies at the Riverside Stadium on August 29.

A fiery south coast derby between Southampton and Portsmouth will be on the box as well.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

Saints, whose boss Tonda Eckert received death threats following Spygate, take on Pompey on October 11.

ITV have also bagged the rights to screen Burnley’s encounter with neighbours Blackburn Rovers on November 22.

The Clarets notched a narrow 1-0 win when the Lancashire foes met last year.

And ITV’s final Championship offering of 2026 will be West Ham’s trip to Birmingham.

Sports.title: England star’s sister follows in his footsteps and signs first professional contract at Premier League giants
Sports.content:
SACHA LEWIS is looking to emulate her brother Rico – after penning her first professional contract with Women’s Super League title holders Manchester City.

The Sky Blues bolstered their squad by landing Beth Mead from Arsenal last month.



And City have now rewarded Lewis, 18, with a deal after showing plenty of promise while coming through the ranks.

The defender has followed in her brother Rico’s footsteps, having seen him make waves in the Premier League before narrowly missing out on a place in England’s World Cup squad.



Lewis is now desperate to play a key role as City aim to defend their WSL crown.

After putting pen-to-paper, the England Under-19s international said: “It’s amazing. A lot of hard work was put in and it’s such a great achievement. I’m proud.

“It means so much, it means even more because I support City. Being here in the academy, not many people get this opportunity so I’m very grateful.”

Lewis joined the Sky Blues’ U14s before working her way through the system and being integrated into the senior squad.

The teenager was rewarded with a place in the matchday squad for two WSL showdowns last season.

And City chief Andree Jeglertz included Lewis among the substitutes for the League Cup semi-final loss to Chelsea in January.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

Director of football Therese Sjogran said: “This is a special moment for Sacha and one she fully deserves.

“Her development is another demonstration of the incredible pathway our young players have to the first team.

“She’s been a shining example to her team-mates despite still being just 18.

“To that point, I would also like to thank our head of girls’ academy Hannah Dingley, lead coach Izzy Christiansen and everyone involved in our Next Gen set-up for their role in Sacha’s development.



“We’re all excited to see what she can achieve at City in the coming years. With her talent and attitude, she certainly has a bright future in the game.”

Sports.title: Ex-Newcastle chief Amanda Staveley ‘in offer to buy David Sullivan’s 38.8% West Ham stake to own MAJORITY 63.9% of club’
Sports.content:
AMANDA STAVELEY reportedly offered to buy David Sullivan’s West Ham stake – and become the majority shareholder.

The former Newcastle co-owner’s firm PCP has the backing of US and Far East-based investors.



And after being the face of the Saudi takeover at St James’ Park, she is keen to spearhead a bid to take control of West Ham following their relegation to the Championship.

As reported by The Football Boardroom, Staveley approached Sullivan to buy out his 38.8 per cent stake in the Hammers for around £228million.



She also approached the Gold family over purchasing their 25.1 per cent at a price of £150m.

Together, that would total 63.9 per cent of the club for £378m.

Should PCP’s bid prove successful, they would become the majority owners of West Ham.

However, Daniel Kretinsky owns 27 per cent through 1890 Holdings and the WHU LLC holds the remaining eight per cent, led by J Albert Smith.

Staveley’s offers would value the entire 100 per cent stake of West Ham at just shy of £600m.

Sullivan could be forced to sell his portion of West Ham with the independent football regulator investigating his position following allegations of sexually exploitative and predatory behaviour.



CASINO SPECIAL – BEST CASINO BONUSES FROM £10 DEPOSITS

Sullivan, 77, denies all allegations and resigned from his position as Joint Chair of the club to fight them.

His former co-owner and business partner David Gold died in January 2023, with his family retaining his 25.1 per cent stake in West Ham.

Daughter Vanessa took control of the Gold stake and revealed in a statement just days ago that she intends to sell them to Staveley’s consortium.

Gold said: “I have now reached an agreement to sell my family’s shareholding to a consortium of PCP Capital Partners, led by Amanda Staveley and Mehrdad Ghodoussi, in partnership with Ashland Forest Capital Partners.



“While the process has not yet concluded, I wanted to be open with our fans about where things stand and my intentions.”

However, Staveley – who was part of the Newcastle takeover in 2021 and remained a shareholder until 2024 – could have seen her hopes dashed.

That is because Kretinsky moved to try and block her buying the Gold shares.

The Czech businessman – who owns Royal Mail – was primed to take control of the club when Sullivan resigned in June.

Kretinsky is a minority owner as it stands – he is also majority owner and president of Sparta Prague.



However, he agreed to buy 16 per cent of West Ham from the Golds to take his stake to 43 per cent – with existing shareholders getting pre-emption rights offered before being opened up externally.

But with Staveley exploring the option of buying out both Gold and Sullivan, that would take her ownership to a majority.

In response, Kretinsky is selling two per cent of the club to fellow Czech Jakub Havrlant.

That means he could then buy the Golds’ 25.1 per cent and stay at the 50 per cent mark – enough to ensure Staveley cannot supercede his ownership without becoming the majority shareholder.

Should he exceed 50 per cent, that may trigger a clause forcing Kretinsky to buy Sullivan’s stake at an inflated price.



Staveley, meanwhile, has made no secret of her ambition to get back into football – and hinted at going for West Ham as well as the land around the London Stadium.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

She told Bloomberg: “Whatever club we take, there will be a big property play as well. We won’t just do a football-led.”

The news came just hours after it was reported that Staveley has failed to settle a £750,000 debt with her former club Newcastle.

Sports.title: Two Champions League rule changes announced by UEFA ahead of new season
Sports.content:
Two Champions League rule changes announced by UEFA ahead of new season

UEFA has updated its regulations and made changes which will affect the nine English clubs playing in either the Champions League, Europa League or Conference League in the 2026-27 season

View 2 Images Qualifying for the 2026-27 Champions League has begun (Image: Kristian Skeie - UEFA/UEFA via Getty Images)

UEFA have announced two rule changes ahead of this season's Champions League. Qualifying for the competition has already started, with the draw for the league phase not until late August.

‌



The same goes for UEFA's other primary competitions, the Conference League and Europa League. And the regulations for each competition have been updated, with two changes announced on Tuesday.

‌



Firstly, the yellow card threshold has been raised. A player will now need four yellow cards rather than three to pick up the first one-match ban.

‌



And secondly, UEFA have removed its long-standing regulation that prevented stadium clocks moving beyond 45 and 90 minutes. This change has been seen in the Premier League for the last two years.

The draw for the Champions League play-off round was made on Monday. Celtic are the only British club involved in the round and will face LASK of Austria in their bid to reach the league phase.

‌



Five English teams will play in the 2026-27 Champions League. Arsenal, Manchester City, Manchester United, Aston Villa and Liverpool qualified through their league position.

In the Europa League, Bournemouth, Crystal Palace and Sunderland will feature. And in the Conference League, which Palace won last season, Brighton are the Premier League's sole representatives.

What do you make of the rule changes? Have your say in the comments section.

‌



View 2 Images Paris Saint-Germain will once again bid to defend their crown (Image: Carl Recine/Getty Images)

UEFA has been in the headlines over the past week after its 55 member nations unanimously voted to pull out of FIFA competitions during an emergency virtual meeting on Friday. It comes after FIFA controversially unveiled plans to sell off its competitions to private investors.

In response, the European body said: "As a result of today's discussion, no UEFA national teams will participate in any FIFA competition for so long as these proposals remain alive, unless this proposal has been abandoned in its entirety and binding assurances have been given that FIFA will never again open its governance or competitions to private ownership."

‌



UEFA invited other confederations to follow their lead and reportedly believe that a number of Asian countries are also against the plan. "National associations around the world are now presented with an ultimatum: accept the irreversible capture of football's greatest competitions or bear the consequences," it added.

"This is not a 'democratic decision', but governance by intimidation - an act of coercion unworthy of an institution entrusted with the stewardship of the global game."

Jose Mourinho has told Arsenal transfer target Vinicius Jr to enjoy himself, be positive and continue playing his style of football. The 25-year-old is back training in the Spanish capital after his break following Brazil's World Cup exit but the focus has instead been on his future amid significant interest from the Gunners.

‌



Vinicius has just one year remaining on his current contract and while there has not been a breakthrough in extension talks for some time, that could be about to change with new discussions set to take place on Wednesday.

‌



As such, Arsenal could be about to learn a definitive transfer outcome over his future with Real's stance clear that he either agrees to extend or is sold this summer.

‌



OPINION Arsenal may be using Vinicius Jr transfer talk as smokescreen for another huge deal by Fasika Zelealem

In the meantime, the forward has been putting in the hard yards alongside his Real team-mates under Mourinho's watchful eye.

In a video posted to Real's official social media channels, he lifted the lid on exactly what the new Los Blancos chief expects from him.

The 26-year-old said: "He wants me to be just as I've always been - happy, positive and playing my own style of football."

Sports.title: Gianni Infantino calls FIFA crisis meeting in desperate attempt to cling to power
Sports.content:
Gianni Infantino calls FIFA crisis meeting in desperate attempt to cling to power

FIFA President Gianni Infantino is under mounting pressure to step down from his role over plans to sell off its competitions, including the World Cup, to private investors

View 2 Images Gianni Infantino's plan is rapidly falling apart (Image: DANIEL DUARTE/AFP via Getty Images)

Under-fire FIFA President Gianni Infantino has called his senior staff to a crisis meeting in a bid to cling to power. The desperate move comes after Arsene Wenger, FIFA's Chief of Global Football Development, broke rank and criticised Infantino's controversial plan to sell off competitions including the World Cup.

‌



Former Arsenal manager Wenger issued a statement on Monday saying that the withdrawal of Infantino's plan was 'absolutely necessary'. Meanwhile, Infantino's close allies are said to have been urging many of the 211 member associations to publicly back him after some withdrew their support for his re-election - while the president of one federation accused him of 'blackmail'.

‌



The Times report that Infantino has called staff to the Moroccan capital of Rabat for a crisis meeting. The Swiss chief is holed up in Morocco amid the swam of backlash.

‌



It's added that a group of senior staff within FIFA had a management meeting on Tuesday - without Infantino. All bar one reportedly opposed the plan to sell off FIFA's competitions.

Gianni Infantino accused of blackmail by Jordan FA chief in brutal FIFA criticism READ MORE :

Full list of Gianni Infantino's supporters and critics as FIFA president faces fight for job READ MORE :

Wenger's comments have also piled on pressure. " The recent events at FIFA deserve some clarity from my side. I was not involved in this strategic plan and first became aware of the project through media reports," the Frenchman said.

"The decision to withdraw the project was absolutely necessary and beyond question, because I firmly believe in an independent FIFA that serves our game with commitment, transparency and integrity."

‌



Even Infantino's No.2, FIFA secretary general Mattias Grafstrom, was revealed to have slammed the plan in a leaked email. " We have all been thrown into the middle of a turmoil, which is difficult to comprehend and accept, but, as Secretary General, I urge you to remain focused on what has always united us: serving football and serving our 211 member associations." Grafstrom wrote.

Should Gianni Infantino step down? Have your say in the comments section.

View 2 Images Arsene Wenger has broken rank and criticised the scheme (Image: Jean Catuffe/Getty Images)

‌



"A sad and reproachable series of events - which were thankfully concluded with the FFE project permanently abandoned - for as much as we feel dismayed by them, should not overshadow this reality.

"I assure you that you as members of the administration, you will be defended and safeguarded from the political context we currently experience. You do not need to worry.

"Individuals, unstable moments and unfortunate episodes come and go. The institution, its mission and its responsibility towards world football continue, and that is why we should always keep our professionalism, sense of perspective and composure."

Sports.content:
Amanda Staveley suffers major blow to West Ham plan as Daniel Kretinsky fights back

The battle for ownership at West Ham United has intensified after Daniel Kretinsky responded to Amanda Staveley’s consortium agreeing a £150m deal with the family of David Gold

View 2 Images Amanda Staveley (Image: (Serena Taylor/Newcastle United via Getty Images))

Amanda Staveley has suffered a blow in her attempt to buy into West Ham United after Daniel Kretinsky agreed to sell just over 2% of his stake in the club to Jakub Havrlant.

‌



Within the last few days, Staveley, her husband Mehrdad Ghodoussi, and others agreed to buy a 25.1 per cent stake in the Hammers, who were relegated to the Championship last season.

‌



Staveley’s consortium agreed a £150million deal with the family of the late David Gold on Saturday. But before Staveley can buy it, existing shareholders have first refusal at the price she agreed.

‌



However, Hammers co-chair Kretinsky sold just over 2% of his stake in the club to Czech businessman Havrlant on Tuesday, dealing a blow to Staveley and her consortium. As a result of the deal, BBC Sport explain Kretinsky can now buy Gold's 25.1% stake without his own stake exceeding 50%, which would otherwise force him to make an offer for the remainder of the club.

"I am delighted Jakub Havrlant has joined the West Ham ownership group as a shareholder, subject to the pre-emption process," Kretinsky said. "He brings exceptional experience as an investor and digital innovator and I have no doubt his involvement will strengthen our club."

She said: “Whatever club we take, there’ll be a big property play as well. We won’t just do a football-led.

“I just want a challenge, and that’s what excites me. That’s where you get value uplift — when you take something from seedling and allow it to grow.”

Royal Mail owner Kretinsky bought 27% of West Ham in 2021 and for his plan he may need the help of the club’s third-largest shareholder, the American billionaire Albert Tripp Smith, who owns 8 per cent. While The Times are reporting that there are set to be two rounds of bidding.

In the first round, shareholders have 30 days to buy their entitlement, which is up to the same proportion as their present holding. And in the second round, any remaining Gold shares can be bought by shareholders who participated in the first round.

Manchester United are in advanced talks with Middlesbrough over the sale of Radek Vitek. The goalkeeper has been in search of regular game time after an impressive loan spell with Bristol City last season.

‌



Vitek, 22, started United's first two pre-season friendlies under Michael Carrick after returning to Old Trafford. But Carrick left him on the bench for the Red Devils' 2-1 victory over Atletico Madrid on Saturday in a hint at his impending departure.

‌

Sports.title: Ex-Arsenal star makes winning return to English football with League Two club
Sports.content:
Ex-Arsenal star makes winning return to English football with League Two club

Vito Mannone, the ex-Arsenal goalkeeper, signed for Crawley Town as a player-coach this summer and he's already been thrust between the posts by boss Colin Kazim-Richards

View 3 Images Vito Mannone made his first appearance in 18 months (Image: Anna Gowthorpe/Shutterstock)

Former Arsenal goalkeeper Vito Mannone kept a clean sheet to help new club Crawley Town beat York City 2-0 on Monday and reach the Carabao Cup first round proper. Mannone, 38, signed for the League Two side as a player-coach in June after spending last season as a free agent while earning his coaching badges.

‌



The Italian got the nod for Crawley's first game of the season, travelling to York's LNER Community Stadium in a preliminary round of the Carabao Cup. Mannone and his team-mates advanced thanks to goals from Gianmarco Di Biase and Danilo Orsi.

‌



The victory booked Crawley a trip to Watford this Saturday. It was Mannone's first competitive appearance since February 2025 with former club Lille.

‌



He was on Arsenal's books for eight years, making a total of 23 first-team appearances. Mannone left the Emirates in 2013 to join Sunderland for £2million, spending the next four seasons at the Stadium of Light before moving to Reading.

FOLLOW OUR ARSENAL FB PAGE! Latest Gunners news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Arsenal star gives honest verdict on Vinicius Junior as transfer hinges on fresh talks READ MORE :

Bruno Guimaraes to Arsenal saga has Newcastle in contention for all-time worst transfer window READ MORE :

He then plied his trade in France after signing for Monaco in 2020, later joining Lorient and finally Lille. Crawley convinced Mannone to make the drop from the French top flight to the fourth tier of English football by handing him a dual role, with the 38-year-old having recently been coaching at Brighton.

‌



Mannone will head up Crawley's goalkeeping department, taking training sessions and leading player development. "I am delighted and proud to take on this role and can't wait to meet everyone at the club and to start working with the staff and players," he said.

"I'll give everything to the cause and hope to pass on my experiences as a player, leading into a successful season."

Crawley's manager, former Premier League striker Colin Kazim-Richards, explained: "To be able to add to my coaching staff, to the club, someone of Vito's calibre is a credit in itself.

"His knowledge, his footballing experiences, playing at the highest level with some of the best coaches in terms of standards, what it actually takes and ideas coming from a country that creates amazing goalkeepers, has really taken us up another level.

Sports.title: Draper in tears amid injury concern during defeat in Montreal
Sports.content:
Jack Draper was left in tears after losing to Terence Atmane as the Brit's long-term arm injury appeared to resurface and hamper him on his return to action at the Canadian Open.

Playing in just his sixth tournament of the year, and a first since pulling out of Wimbledon, Draper was beaten 6-3 2-6 6-2 by France's Atmane.

After a rusty start, Draper appeared to have found form as he dominated the second set, but his performance suddenly dropped off in the decider as the power in his serves and groundstrokes reduced massively.

When trailing 4-1, Draper sat down and spent the entire changeover crying, apparently uncontrollably.

The 24-year-old carried on and almost claimed a break before spiritedly holding serve one more time, before Atmane closed out victory in an hour and 52 minutes.

Draper had established himself as one of the biggest challengers to Carlos Alcaraz and Jannik Sinner's dominance of the men's game as he moved up to a career high No 4 ranking in June 2025.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the first round match at the Canadian Open between Terence Atmane and Jack Draper.

It was around that time that Draper began suffering from a bone bruise in his left arm, an injury that has continued to hamper him ever since.

In 2026, he put together runs to the quarter-finals at Indian Wells in March and the semi-finals at Eastbourne in June, but has been unable to stay on the court consistently.

Sir Andy Murray has been part of Draper's coaching team since May, but Montreal was just the second tournament he has been able to play in during their partnership.

Draper has a wild card into next week's Cincinnati Open, but his defeat in Montreal is likely to raise fresh doubts over his participation there and at the US Open.

Croft: Very upsetting to see

Sky Sports pundit Annabel Croft, who was commentating on the match, said it was "very upsetting" to see Draper in such distress.

Responding immediately to Draper's tears, Croft said: "This is pretty emotional. He's bent over and literally erupting with emotion here. It's very, very upsetting to see."

"And it was very obvious very quickly that he was not going after big serves, he was rolling them in. He hasn't really hit a serve since, and hasn't really gone after any too many ground strokes either."

There was more disappointing injury news for the ATP Tour as Carlos Alcaraz withdrew from the Cincinnati Open as he continues his recovery from a right wrist injury.

The Spaniard's withdrawal raises doubts over whether he will be ready to defend his US Open title when the final major of the year begins on August 30.
