He added: “There hasn’t been any conversation. We have Virgil [van Dijk] as the captain, we have Ali [Alisson], we have Joe Gomez [as vice-captains], so there was no conversation at all. Obviously Ali is not here and Joe is injured. Let’s see. It’s not fixed. If you get offered the vice-captain of Liverpool, you’re going to take it. It would be a proud moment for me but I respect everybody. Whoever it’s going to be, we’re going to follow them.”

The captain’s armband became an issue for Curtis Jones when Szoboszlai passed it to Kostas Tsimikas during the win over Wrexham in New York. But Szoboszlai, who recently signed a new five-year contract at Anfield, insisted there was no problem with his fellow midfielder.

“It was never a debate between us three,” he claimed. “We just discussed something on the pitch. After, you guys make it very big. But next time we will manage to do it in the changing room. Nobody was angry. It’s all cleared. We are cool, everybody.”

Sports.title: WWE legend Brock Lesnar, 49, announces retirement as SummerSlam loss marks end of 26-year career
Sports.content:
See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

WWE legend Brock Lesnar has called time on his 26-year career in the business following his defeat to Oba Femi at SummerSlam at the weekend.

Lesnar, a wrestling great and former MMA star, made the announcement during an appearance on ESPN's The Pat McAfee Show on Tuesday.

Following his Hell in a Cell loss to Femi at SummerSlam in Minneapolis, the 10-time WWE champion confirmed the time has finally come for him to bow out.

'I’m here today to let the world know that I am retired and I wanted to say a big thank you to everybody,' he told WWE commentator McAfee and his co-host AJ Hawk. 'Saturday was a very emotional day for me.'

Lesnar, 49, has retired from wrestling and returned in the past, while he appeared to suggest the end was coming after leaving his gloves and boots in the center of the ring in an emotional moment after his WrestleMania 42 match against Femi earlier this year.

Yet despite having enough left to compete again at SummerSlam, he insists that defeat in Minneapolis will go down as his last in the business.

WWE icon Brock Lesnar has announced he is calling time on his 26-year career in the business

Lesnar, a 10-time WWE champion, made the announcement on ESPN's The Pat McAfee Show

'I still had some fuel in the tank, but Saturday for Brock Lesnar, that's it. That's it for me in the squared circle and for everything else too,' Lesnar added.

'So I just wanted to give a shout-out to everybody in this universe that has followed me since I was a little kid, all the way till Saturday.'

Lesnar began life with the WWE back in 2002, following a successful college wrestling career that saw him a two-time NJCAA All-American and accrue a staggering 106-5 record over four years.

After signing with the wrestling promotion, he worked his way into the main roster and eventually became one of the biggest stars in the organization.

However, his first stint in the WWE would come to an end in 2004. Following a defeat at WrestleMania XX, he cited burnout, injuries and creative dissatisfaction as his reasons for walking away.

Lesnar returned to the promotion in 2012 and earned a number of WWE championship titles before seemingly retiring at WrestleMania 36.

That decision, however, was short-lived and he returned to the ring in 2021 rocking a new 'cowboy' look that featured a beard and ponytail.

The wrestling great has opted to bow out following his loss to Oba Femi at SummerSlam

In 2023, Lesnar was named in a bombshell sex trafficking lawsuit against WWE co-founder Vince McMahon, filed by his former employee Janel Grant.

As a result of the lawsuit, he was removed from the WWE roster and wiped from their event plans. He would endure a two-year exile from the organization.

He returned at Summer Slam in August 2025, despite the Grant lawsuit remaining active at the time. He took part in a handful of fights between then and Sunday night, before officially retiring from the sport a year later.

Though he's best-known for his time in the squared circle, Lesnar also found success away from wrestling. After leaving WWE for the first time in 2004, he attempted to embark on a professional football career.

Lesnar participated in the NFL Scouting Combine at the time but later suffered a broken jaw and hand from a motorcycle accident which put his progress on hold.

Despite the injuries, a number of NFL teams still held an interest in Lesnar and, in July 2004, he signed with the Minnesota Vikings as a defensive tackle. However, his time with the franchise was short-lived and he was eventually released in August.

After his dreams of being on the gridiron came crashing down, he then decided to try his hand - literally - at mixed martial arts.

Lesnar also enjoyed success as an MMA star over the course of his extraordinary career

He began fighting for a promotion known as 'K-1', in April 2006, and won his first bout via submission in the first round - bring global attention to his MMA skills.

Lesnar would eventually sign with Dana White's UFC in 2008, which proved to be a massive success for the organization given his national star power.

Despite losing his first fight, UFC chief White stuck by Lesnar and offered him a multi-fight deal. Again, this proved to a wise call as Lesnar would later become the UFC heavyweight champion following a win over Randy Couture in November 2008.

In total, he had eight UFC fights, winning four of them and losing three - with the final bout being ruled as a no-contest after he tested positive for clomiphene.

Sports.title: NFL star is removed from practice after throwing a punch just weeks after landing $105m contract
Sports.content:
NFL star is removed from practice after throwing a punch just weeks after landing $105m contract

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Tennessee Titans star Jeffery Simmons was ejected from practice on Tuesday after throwing a punch early in a team drill.

As a result of the violent scenes, the All-Pro defensive tackle was forced to spend the rest of practice working on a side field with a strength coach.

First-year head coach Robert Saleh stopped practice after the incident, pulling his Titans together on the field for a reminder to spend the second session in pads working and not fighting.

'Our policy is if you throw a punch you're ejected in the game, same thing with practice,' Saleh said.

'If you throw punch, you're out of practice. But rather than going to the locker room, he went to the other field. He still got his work in. So the projected reps and the work that he would have gotten, he got in off to the side.'

Simmons, who got a very big extension in late June, also had a brief tussle Monday in the Titans' first day in pads.

Tennessee Titans star Jeffery Simmons was ejected from practice after throwing a punch

Simmons, who got a big extension in June, also had a brief tussle during Monday's practice

Robert Saleh stopped practice and sent his defensive star to practice on his own in Nashville

On Tuesday, Simmons and center Austin Schlottman scuffled after a play before he swung at right tackle JC Latham. Assistant defensive line coach Tanzel Smart grabbed Simmons and took him down out of the scrum.

The Titans went 3-14 last season, and too many penalties for 1,011 yards didn't help.

Latham had the most with 14 penalties, including eight that stalled drives. Simmons ranked second with 12.

Saleh said he wants both lines playing with an edge up to toeing the line.

'We're always going to toe a line of being aggressive and call it instigating if you want,' Saleh said.

'It's just the nature of who we're going to be. But we've got to be disciplined enough to make sure that we always find our way back to the huddle without giving the other team freebies.'

In another concerning moment, left tackle Dan Moore Jr. walked off the field with a trainer.

Saleh had no immediate update after practice. Moore was one of the Titans' big free agent signees in 2025 and a key player for a line already looking for new starters at center and right guard.

Titans quarterback Cam Ward gave fans the play they had been hoping to see late in practice when he threw deep with Carnell Tate, the fourth overall draft pick, running under the ball in the end zone for a 65-yard touchdown.

Sports.title: Mohamed Salah closes in on Turkey move: Trabzonspor confirm talks with former Liverpool star who will fly in TODAY ahead of signing a two-year contract
Sports.content:
Mohamed Salah closes in on Turkey move: Trabzonspor confirm talks with former Liverpool star who will fly in TODAY ahead of signing a two-year contract

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Trabzonspor are closing in on a two-year deal with former Liverpool forward Mo Salah.

The Turkish club's rivals Besiktas were understood to be the Egyptian's first choice but talks with them stalled last week.

On Tuesday night, Trabzonspor shared a brief message with their 1.9million followers on X, with the club writing: 'Public Announcement: Negotiations have begun regarding the transfer of professional footballer Mohamed Salah to our Club.'

The club then posted: 'Professional footballer Mohamed Salah, with whom we have begun transfer negotiations, will be at Istanbul Atatürk Airport General Aviation Terminal at 12:00 on Wednesday, August 5.

'The player is scheduled to arrive in Trabzon on the same day in the evening hours.

'The time and other details regarding the welcome program in Trabzon will be shared with the public through our club's official communication channels during the day.'

Mohammed Salah is closing in on a move to Trabzonspor in Turkey

Trabzonspor also shared a 17-second AI video of a camera shot panning from pyramids over mountains to a view of their 41,000-seater stadium Papara Park.

Salah's future has been the subject of huge interest since the surprising decision was announced back in March that he would leave Liverpool one year into his two-year contract extension.

Many anticipated that Saudi Arabia would be the most likely destination after Al-Ittihad made a £150million bid in summer 2023.

But Trabzonspor are now set to sign the winger, who fell out with Arne Slot at Anfield last term.

The Turkish side finished third last season behind Fenerbahce and champions Galatasaray.

Salah, who is the third-highest goalscorer in Reds history with 255, did not engage in talks with teams before the end of the season out of respect to the Merseyside club.

His long-serving agent, Ramy Abbas, repeatedly insisted nothing had been decided and reaffirmed that stance during the World Cup.

But since returning from the competition in the US, talks have accelerated with interested parties.

Salah, pictured returning to Egypt after the World Cup, looks set to sign a two-year deal

Salah is renowned for his remarkable professionalism and will back himself to remain at a high level deep into his thirties.

Salah was the star man as Slot’s side won the Premier League in Slot's first season, the Egyptian's second English title, but his level dipped last term with just 10 goals last term compared to a staggering 34 when he spear-headed the 2024-25 title win.

Liverpool are yet to replace the player who was voted Professional Footballers' Association (PFA) Players' Player of the Year three times at the club.

With the start of the season fast approaching, Bradley Barcola of PSG remains the most likely high-profile attacking signing.

But the 23-year-old, valued at £145million by his club, plays predominantly on the left and Jamie Carragher recently warned against buying him as a replacement for Salah.

Salah would be the most high-profile signing in Trabzonspor's history and if his expected move is confirmed, will join Man United loanee Andre Onana.

Ex-Man City defender Stefan Savic also plays for the Turkish side, who have won their domestic title seven times.

Sports.title: Gianni Infantino chairs crisis talks with FIFA staff in Morocco as pressure mounts on embattled president after being accused of BLACKMAIL by head of Jordan FA
Sports.content:
Gianni Infantino chairs crisis talks with FIFA staff in Morocco as pressure mounts on embattled president after being accused of BLACKMAIL by head of Jordan FA

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Gianni Infantino has summoned senior FIFA officials to a hotel in Morocco for crisis talks as pressure continues to mount on the FIFA president.

It comes after Jordan FA president Prince Ali bin Hussein accused him of blackmail.

Infantino has come under intense scrutiny since plans to sell £3.1billion in World Cup stakes leaked last week.

The Swiss football administrator has since scrapped the proposals after widespread opposition – including an internal rebellion at FIFA.

UEFA and CONCACAF – the body for North and Central America and the Caribbean – are both calling for Infantino to step down, with Europe declaring a lack of confidence in the FIFA president.

Jordan, meanwhile, are the first Asian nation to rebel against Infantino – taking the total to 91, assuming all UEFA and CONCACAF nations follow the stance set by their continental bodies. 106 nations are needed to depose Infantino as president.

In a statement Hussein ripped into Infantino, accusing him of delaying prize money payments and refusing to address the problem unless Jordan endorsed him for a fourth term at the helm of world football.

Gianni Infantino has summoned senior FIFA officials to a hotel in Morocco for crisis talks

Infantino has been accused of blackmail by Jordan FA president Prince Ali bin Hussein

‘There is no shortage of issues regarding FIFA. Let me start by clarifying what some of these are from an FA perspective, in particular that of Jordan going into a World Cup for the first time,’ Hussein said.

‘We are a small country with a minimal budget for our FA and had to deal with enormous hurdles.

‘First, getting our fans into the USA: not all were granted visas, even though they had tickets - which we also know were sold at exorbitant prices.

‘Secondly, we are being taxed by the US government through FIFA for our participation. Money that should go to players and staff.

‘This was not the case for those who played and set up camp in Canada and Mexico. But we happened to be in the USA so now we face these huge costs in taxes for having participated.

‘Thirdly we have been waiting for reward money for our players since December for the Arab Cup in Qatar, which is a FIFA event.

‘The money our team should receive for having reached the final has not been delivered yet, while at the same time FIFA brags about how many billions they have in reserve.

‘It is clear the problem really is with leadership. For months, FIFA has been refusing to help us on any of these or other matters - until it was verbally communicated to me during the World Cup that if I endorsed Infantino it would go a long way to helping our FA out.

‘We pride ourselves in Jordan in upholding ethical values. We did not endorse him before and certainly will not now.

‘But the whole situation amounts to blackmail and we refuse to give in to that.’

Daily Mail Sport have contacted FIFA for comment.

Sports.title: Jack Draper breaks down in tears as Brit loses on return from injury at Canadian Open
Sports.content:
Jack Draper breaks down in tears as Brit loses on return from injury at Canadian Open

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Jack Draper's torturous attempts to return to tennis continued as he wiped away tears during defeat in the first round of the Canadian Open.

Trailing Frenchman Terence Atmane 4-1 in the deciding set, the British former world No4 sat in his chair at the changeover and wept.

It was a truly wretched sight and, while we must wait for the man himself to speak, it seems likely those tears were an indication that he is still feeling the pain of an arm injury which simply will not leave him alone.

Some natural ring-rust aside, there was nothing much wrong with Draper’s level in the first two sets, and when he won the second comfortably he looked well placed to take the match. But his serve began to subside dramatically and by the end he could do little more than just roll it over. The 24-year-old also, in apparent desperation, started to hit an increasing number of dropshots.

Atmane, in terrible form himself, won 6-3, 2-6, 6-2.

It has been well over 12 months now that Draper has struggled with bone bruising in the humerus of his left arm.

Jack Draper was in tears during the third set of his game against Terence Atmane in Montreal as he continues his return from injury 🎾 pic.twitter.com/ekhBse3Af3 — Sky Sports Tennis (@SkySportsTennis) August 4, 2026

Jack Draper was reduced to tears as he lost his comeback match following time out with injury

The British former world No 4 sat in his chair at the changeover and wept in the final set

Due to play at Wimbledon, he pulled out the day before his match. Set to return in Washington, he withdrew citing a twinge in that arm.

The injury is clearly chronic and, if this is indeed yet another setback, it is not easy to see where Draper goes from here.

Draper said earlier this week: 'It's important for people to recognise that the injury I have is very complex, it's very complicated and everyone around me is doing everything we can to help this keep moving along.

'It's not as simple as 'rest and heal up and you'll come back and you'll be fine'.

Terribly sad to say, it is becoming increasingly likely we may never see the best of this beautifully, brutally brilliant player again.

Sports.title: Liverpool consider move for 18-year-old PSG winger Ibrahim Mbaye - as well as his team-mate Bradley Barcola
Sports.content:
Liverpool are assessing whether to make an approach for PSG winger Ibrahim Mbaye - as well as his teammate Bradley Barcola.

Mbaye is an 18-year-old right winger who starred for Senegal at the World Cup.

Liverpool have been among the clubs made aware of the teenager's availability earlier in the window, but Manchester City and Tottenham were understood to have shown greater interest.

However, it is Bundesliga side Bayer Leverkusen who have been making the greater progress.

Now with concerns about the squad’s capability and lack of goal-power, Liverpool are considering an approach for both PSG flyers.

Mbaye would at least be a more natural fit to replace Mo Salah who left Anfield and is closing on a move to Trabzonspor while Barcola prefers the left.

Ibrahim Mbaye, pictured in action for Senegal at the World Cup, is an option for Liverpool

Much will depend on the asking price as PSG would likely ask for over £150m.

The situation is expected to become clearer in the coming days as the clubs maintain dialogue.

Mbaye is represented by agent Jorge Mendes.

The 6ft 1in winger has been at PSG since 2018 and made 33 appearances for the senior side, scoring four times.

He represented France at youth level before pledging his international allegiance to Senegal in 2025.

Mbaye was a bright light for his country at the World Cup in the US and became the youngest African scorer in tournament history when he netted a consolation against France.

Liverpool are looking to bolster their attacking ranks, though Cody Gakpo has emerged as a target for Tottenham.

But the club have no plans to sell the Dutch international Gakpo despite the north London side making their interest known.

Gakpo, 27, is contracted until 2030 and with current market prices escalating for players of his experience, it would take a huge sum to change Liverpool's stance.

The Dutchman had a weaker season than usual last time out, scoring only nine goals, but is highly valued by Liverpool all the same. His best season, 2024-25, saw him bang in 18 goals.

Trabzonspor are hopeful of agreement over a two year deal with Mo Salah

Fulham lodge new £25m bid for Saints star

Fulham have made a revised £25million offer for Southampton midfielder Shea Charles.

The Championship side rejected Fulham's first bid for the Northern Ireland international but the Cottagers have improved their proposal with add-ons on top.

Fresh from signing £46million Real Madrid duo Gonzalo Garcia and Cesar Palacios, manager Alvaro Arbeloa wants Fulham to strengthen further with the former Manchester City midfielder.

Leeds United walked away from talks for Charles last month after making what they felt were reasonable offers for the 22-year-old.

Fulham have made a revised £25million offer for Southampton midfielder Shea Charles

Southampton have been digging in their heels pushing for £30m but Charles wants to go for the chance to play in the Premier League which he missed out on in May.

Fulham remain talks to add Thiago Pitarch from Real Madrid too.

Hull move for Norway youth star

Hull City are finalising a £7million deal for 20-year-old Norwegian midfielder Jens Hjerto-Dahl from Tromso.

The U21 international set off for England this morning ahead of his medical and agreeing terms.

As Daily Mail Sport reported on Sunday, Hull have beaten off competition from Rangers and Cardiff City.

Ipswich target Brazilian centre back

Ipswich Town are interested in Real Betis centre back Natan.

The 25-year-old joined from Napoli last season and was on the brink of making Carlo Ancelotti's World Cup squad but ultimately missed out.

Ipswich Town are interested in Real Betis's 25-year-old Braziliann centre back Natan.

Ipswich, meanwhile have signed midfielder Florentino from Burnley on a five-year contract.

As Daily Mail Sport reported, the fee is an initial £16m plus a further £3m in add-ons.

Hull City had been in advanced talks over an initial loan for the 26-year-old.

Palace swoop for teenage US defender

Crystal Palace are closing on an £11million deal for Real Salt Lake wing-back Zavier Gozo.

The 19-year-old is a USA U23 international and can play as a right wing-back or right winger.

The teenager has also attracted interest from Lyon and Hoffenheim but is heading for Palace as talks progress.

Man United keeper making Middlesbrough move

Middlesbrough are closing in on the permanent signing of Manchester United goalkeeper Radek Vitek as the ambitious Championship side look to win promotion to the Premier League.

Czech goalkeeper Vitek was a huge success in the second tier last season with Bristol City and despite returning to United for pre-season, he made it plain he wants to go out and be a No 1.

United signed Karl Darlow to act as back-up to No 1 Senne Lammens and Vitek's future is now coming in to sharp focus with a deal to join Middlesbrough close to completion.

Middlesbrough are closing in on the permanent signing of Manchester United goalkeeper Radek Vitek

Daily Mail Sport understands United are satisfied with the deal, not least because a buy-back clause has been inserted into the agreement and there are a number of other clauses which United believe favour them in the move.

Speaking after defeat by Wrexham in Helsinki earlier this summer, Vitek expressed how important it is for him to go out and be the main man.

'I'm ready to go somewhere again and hopefully be No 1,' he said.

'My mind is the same [as it was back in March]. I want to play every week and that's the goal for next season.'

Middlesbrough are one of the leading contenders to win promotion from the Championship next season having also struck a £20million agreement with Tottenham Hotspur for striker Will Lankshear.

NATHAN SALT

Man City step up Neto pursuit

Manchester City are firming up their interest in Chelsea winger Pedro Neto, after Daily Mail Sport first reported their interest last month.

Chelsea want over £65million for the Portuguese international who cost them £51m from Wolves.

City also made enquiries to sign him at the time.

Manchester City are firming up their interest in Chelsea winger Pedro Neto

They want a winger in with Tottenham keen to sign Savinho.

Bristol City splash the cash for Ballard

Bristol City are finalising the £5million signing of Leyton Orient striker Dom Ballard.

Protracted negotiations came to a conclusion today as ambitious City upped their offer for the 21-year-old.

Ballard scored 23 league goals last season and City will now team him with their other signing Lorent Tolaj, who scored 17 goals for Plymouth last season, in a potentially explosive partnership.

Southampton also have a sell-on percentage on Ballard who was named in the League One Team of the season, named Player of the Season and Young Player of the Season at the EFL Awards in May.

Chelsea close to new defender

Chelsea are closing on agreement with Rayo Vallecano for left wing-back Pep Chavarria.

The 28-year-old is waiting for permission to travel for a medical as final details are being ironed out.

Chelsea are closing on agreement with Rayo Vallecano for left wing-back Pep Chavarria

Toon continue Nmecha pursuit

Newcastle are continuing to explore a move for Germany international Felix Nmecha.

Daily Mail Sport reported Newcastle's interest earlier in the window and he remains a player they rate very highly but the asking price is around £78million for the 25-year-old.

The Borussia Dortmund midfielder also attracted enquiries from Manchester United but they have other priorities.

Newcastle need a top signing with Arsenal nearing total agreement to sign captain Bruno Guimaraes.

Both sides are keen to get the saga wrapped up as talks reach a conclusion on the final fee and payment structure for the 28-year-old Brazilian.

Reijnders a £55m target for Forest

Manchester City midfielder Tijjani Reijnders has emerged as a £55million target for Nottingham Forest.

The Netherlands international is understood to be open to the move for the chance of regular first-team football and would be a key figure in Oliver Glasner's plans.

Read more on this story HERE.

Tijjani Reijnders joined Manchester City last summer but wants to be a regular starter

Esse does it as Palace say no

Crystal Palace have rebuffed an initial approach from Club Brugge for Romain Esse.

The Belgian side's target list also includes KRC Genk's Noah Adedeji-Sternberg and Red Bull Salzburg's Edmund Baidoo.

Esse spent part of last season on loan at Coventry City.

Romain Esse in action against Famelicao in Como last week

Villa ask Atletico about Ruggeri

Aston Villa have asked about Atletico Madrid left-back Matteo Ruggeri.

The 24-year-old former Italy U21 international only joined Atletico last summer from Atalanta. He made 26 appearances in La Liga and 47 overall.

Atletico would consider suitable offers if Ruggeri wished to pursue the move.

Villa want a replacement for Lucas Digne and had previously pursued Pervis Estupinan of AC Milan but Ruben Amorim wanted to have a closer look at him in pre-season before deciding on his future.

Villa have also made a check on the availability of Marseille winger Igor Paixao, who is also on Leeds United's list.

Matteo Ruggeri in pre-season action against Manchester United's Leny Yoro last weekend

Spurs look at Chelsea striker Jackson

Tottenham Hotspur are interested in Chelsea striker Nicolas Jackson.

There has been no formal approach to open club-to-club talks yet, it is understood, but sources have confirmed to Daily Mail Sport that Spurs have the 25-year-old Senegalese under consideration.

Read more on this story HERE

KIERAN GILL

Norgaard heads north

Arsenal have given Christian Norgaard permission to have a medical with Everton, as reported by Daily Mail Sport.

The midfielder has not travelled with Arsenal's squad to Dublin ahead of his proposed £7million move to Everton.

While Brazilians Gabriel and Gabriel Martinelli are part of the squad in Dublin after returning post World Cup, players involved in the England, Spain, Norway and France squads are still off.

Christian Norgaard is undergoing a medical ahead of his move to Everton

Now bring on the Premier League, says Rushworth after Coventry move

Coventry have confirmed the £22.5million signing of goalkeeper Carl Rushworth from Brighton.

Rushworth, who is represented by former Reading and Ireland winger now agent Stephen Hunt, spent last season on loan at Coventry, winning the Championship's Golden Glove Award after keeping 17 clean sheets and helping the club get promoted to the Premier League as champions.

Newcastle United also showed interest in Rushworth, who has signed a five-year contract.

Rushworth said: 'There's so many emotions that I've got. I can finally relax knowing it's done and that I'm back with the boys and at a club I loved being at.'

Carl Rushworth enjoyed a successful Championship campaign with Coventry

Derby want midfielder Tom Iorpenda from Huddersfield.

The 21-year-old is keen to make the move to the Championship after an impressive season on loan with Notts County last time out, where he caught the eye of Derby staff.

He scored three goals and provided seven assists in his season in League Two helping Notts County to promotion via the play-offs.

Iorpenda, who started out at Brighton, won Notts County's Players' player of the season award, Fans' player of the season award and Goal of the season to underline the impact he made.

The Hammers said: 'Everyone at West Ham United would like to sincerely thank Freddie for his hard work, commitment and all-round contribution and wish him every success in the future.'

Sports.title: Iconic WWE Hall of Fame wrestler dead at 85 as tributes pour in
Sports.content:
Iconic WWE Hall of Fame wrestler dead at 85 as tributes pour in

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

WWE Hall of Famer Dory Funk Jr has died at the age of 85, prompting a wave of tributes across the professional wrestling community.

Triple H announced Funk's passing on Tuesday, honoring the legend's in-ring style and the impact he made on the industry during his decades-long career.

'From the Double Cross Ranch to the WWE Hall of Fame, Dory's style inspired countless performers in our industry,' Triple H wrote in a tribute on social media.

'Whether it was at WrestleMania 2, WCW, ECW, or the dozens of NWA-affiliated promotions, his travels across North America and Asia were a part of the early blueprint that helped build this business into a global phenomenon.'

Funk began his professional wrestling career in 1963 and reached the pinnacle of the sport in 1969 when he captured the NWA World Heavyweight Championship.

He held the title for over four years, marking the second-longest uninterrupted reign in the belt's history.

WWE Hall of Famer Dory Funk Jr. has died at the age of 85

Funk began his professional wrestling career in 1963 and reached the pinnacle of the sport in 1969 when he captured the NWA World Heavyweight Championship

Alongside his younger brother, Terry Funk, who passed away in August 2023 at age 79, Dory made history as part of the only pair of siblings to both hold the NWA World Heavyweight Championship.

The duo wrestled together worldwide, including a notable tag-team appearance at WrestleMania 2, before being inducted together into the WWE Hall of Fame in 2009.

Beyond his accomplishments in the ring, Funk was instrumental in shaping the next generation of sports entertainment stars, spending decades training future legends such as Kurt Angle, Edge, Christian Cage and the Hardy Boyz.

'A hard-nosed and fierce competitor, his rugged in-ring style was only eclipsed by the decades he spent training athletes to perform in the squared circle he loved so much,' Triple H added.

'My thoughts and those of the entire WWE Universe are with his loved ones during this difficult time.'

Sports.title: Tony Bloom's Royal Ascot heroine ruled out for rest of season after injury blow
Sports.content:
Tony Bloom's Royal Ascot heroine ruled out for rest of season after injury blow

Commonwealth Cup winner Venetian Sun has been ruled out for the rest of the season after trainer Karl Burke confirmed the sprinter has suffered a tendon injury

View 3 Images Tony Bloom (second left) with Venetian Sun, who followed up her success at Royal Ascot with a Group 1 victory in France (Image: PA)

Tony Bloom's Royal Ascot heroine Venetian Sun has suffered an injury setback that will sideline her for the remainder of the campaign.

‌



Among last year's top juveniles, the lightning-quick daughter of Starman – owned by Brighton & Hove Albion chairman in partnership with Ian McAleavy – has maintained her brilliant form this season, claiming a second Royal Ascot triumph when storming to Commonwealth Cup glory.

‌



Her most recent outing saw her produce an excellent runner-up effort against older rivals at Newmarket in the July Cup, and she had been under consideration for a trip to France for this weekend's Prix Maurice de Gheest at Deauville, the venue where she captured the Prix Morny as a two-year-old.

‌



Rossa Ryan convinces BHA panel to reduce 28-day ban to 10 days at appeal hearing READ MORE :

Saffie Osborne to captain Ryan Moore and Dylan Browne McMonagle in Shergar Cup at Ascot READ MORE :

Nevertheless, plans for the remainder of her three year old campaign have been shelved following the discovery of a tendon problem.

Her trainer Karl Burke said: "It's a big shame and unfortunately it happens. It's a long way from being a career- or life-threatening injury, but obviously is going to take time and it's very disappointing.

"We had more or less decided to swerve Deauville anyway because the ground was very fast out there last weekend with no sign of any rain and the French not watering like they used to do.

‌



View 3 Images Celebrations on the track after Venetian Sun's Royal Ascot victory (Image: Getty Images)

"It's just one of those things, we have a feeling she may have initiated it at Newmarket during the July Cup but she came back from there with a nasty little cut and she had been on antibiotics and anti-inflammatories and we think that may have masked it to a degree."

Venetian Sun has triumphed in six of her nine career starts to date, with her connections eagerly anticipating an autumn schedule that could have featured appearances in Haydock's Sprint Cup, at Ascot on British Champions Day and at the Breeders' Cup.

‌



Explaining the setback, Burke added: "It's basically a strain to the tendon, it happens a lot with jumping horses – it's unusual really at this stage in a sprinter's life, but can happen.

View 3 Images Venetian Sun sprinted to victory at Ascot (Image: Martin Dokoupil/ZUMA Press Wire/Shutterstock)

"It's a time thing now and she will have the next six or seven months on the easy list and then be reassessed from there.

Article continues below

"The little bit of work she has done the last few days has just aggravated it and we've had the vets in this morning and they weren't 100 per cent happy with a little bit of heat in the leg and that is what it turns out to be.

"The plan before today was if she finished the season in good shape she would stay in training and that may still be the plan, but that is a discussion for later on."

Sports.title: Harry Kane extending his Bayern stay is a no-brainer - and Ballon d'Or could play big part
Sports.content:
Harry Kane extending his Bayern stay is a no-brainer - and Ballon d'Or could play big part

The England captain will head back to his club in the next few days and Bayern will immediately resume talks over a new contract that will keep the striker in the Bundesliga beyond 2027

View 3 Images Harry Kane has had three very productive seasons with Bayern Munich (Image: Alex Grimm/Getty Images)

Just over nine years ago, Harry Kane mildly surprised a small gathering of reporters when he declared winning the Ballon d’Or to be one of his prime ambitions. Nothing wrong with aiming high, of course. But, at the time, Kane was a 23-year-old striker who had made 17 appearances for his country and had scored five goals.

‌



His numbers with Spurs were very good - 78 goals in 113 Premier League appearances - but he had only been an established top-flight player for three seasons. But Kane believed in himself and lifting that Ballon d’Or is a realistic prospect when the awards ceremony, for the first time in its history, comes to London in October.

‌



Carabao Cup draw confirmed as final fixtures announced for round one READ MORE :

Gianni Infantino ripped apart as explosive FIFA email leaked after botched World Cup plan READ MORE :

Bookmakers do not normally get these sorts of things wrong and every odds-maker has Kane as the favourite to become the seventh British player to receive the accolade. The influence of the World Cup, though, should not be under-estimated.

‌



Some of the 100 journalists who make the choice could well forgive Rodri an injury-interrupted and otherwise mediocre season with his club for his imperious role in Spain’s summer triumph. Lamine Yamal and Kylian Mbappe would appear to be the only other realistic contenders.

And they are worthy contenders. If Kane does not win the 2026 edition, he will have the award in his sights for next year - a year with no major international tournaments.

And if he stays at Bayern Munich, goals are a guarantee. In three seasons in Germany, he has 146 in 147 appearances. If he moved to Barcelona - a switch that seems slightly fanciful but has been mooted reasonably strongly - goals would be a guarantee.

‌



View 3 Images Rodri won the Ballon d'Or in 2024 and is a strong contender for this year's award (Image: Getty Images)

Kane is not coming back to the Premier League any time soon, we can be fairly certain of that. He will report back for training with Bayern after the Bundesliga champions have returned from a pre-season trip to Korea and Hong Kong on Saturday.

Contract talks will immediately resume, as his current deal expires in the summer of 2027. And quite frankly, it is hard to see why Kane would not want to extend his agreement.

‌



He could ask for a release clause at the end of next season if he feels he might have the urge to come back and break the Premier League goalscoring record - he is currently 47 short of Alan Shearer’s total of 260 - but he seems extremely content in Bavaria. Plus, the style of play, the quality of play, the guarantee of competing for honours on all fronts, are all factors that will help him stay in top shape for the international challenges that still lie ahead, most notably leading England into Euro 2028.

He turned 33 a week ago but Kane has looked a better, all-round player for his time in Munich. He was certainly more impressive for England at World Cup 2026 than he was at either Euro 2024 or World Cup 2022. He is not unusual but playing in a dominant team suits him.

View 3 Images Harry Kane has plenty of international challenges left despite his World Cup disappointment (Image: Getty Images)

‌



When he sits down with his advisers and the Bayern hierarchy in the next week, there will, of course, be no escaping the relevance of his age. But over the past few years, the longevity of marquee players - and of strikers, in particular - will have probably had a bearing on his plans.

Since his 34th birthday, Kane’s predecessor at Bayern, Robert Lewandowski, has scored 125 club goals. Kane could return to the Premier League as a 35-year-old - in two seasons’ time - and still fancy his chances of beating Shearer’s number.

But before then, he will have his eyes on another individual accolade. And if the Ballon d’Or does not come his way on the 70th anniversary of the award (the first one, in 1956, was won by Stanley Matthews, hence why the ceremony is in London), you can guarantee he will be a contender again if he stays at Bayern Munich. The Premier League and Shearer’s record are going to have to wait.

Sports.title: Ex-Premier League referee Anthony Taylor lands new job in football following retirement
Sports.content:
Ex-Premier League referee Anthony Taylor lands new job in football following retirement

Anthony Taylor called time on his refereeing career last month, but he's already found a new position that will see him take his wealth of experience as a match official abroad

View 2 Images Anthony Taylor retired after 20-year refereeing career (Image: Ayman Aref/NurPhoto via Getty Images)

Anthony Taylor has landed a new job in football just weeks after announcing his retirement from professional refereeing. The former Premier League match official has been appointed the director of elite refereeing for the Turkish Football Federation (TFF).

‌



Taylor, 47, hung up his whistle after his last match at this summer's World Cup, taking charge of Spain's 1-0 win against Portugal in the round of 16. But now he's back in football with the TFF.

‌



"I am delighted to be joining the Turkish Football Federation and very much looking forward to beginning this new role," Taylor said. "Elite refereeing has been at the centre of my professional life for many years, and this appointment gives me the opportunity to use that experience in a different way."

‌



His appointment comes 10 months after the conclusion of a five-year investigation which found that 371 of 571 match officials in Turkey had betting accounts. TFF president Ibrahim Haciosmanoglu stated at the time: "If we want to bring Turkish football to the place it deserves, we have to clean up whatever dirt there is."

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Gianni Infantino ripped apart as explosive FIFA email leaked after botched World Cup plan READ MORE :

Some of the clean-up job will be given to Taylor, who refereed 831 matches over a 20-year career. "I am excited by the Federation's ambitions for its match officials and by the opportunity to help shape the strategic and technical development of its refereeing programme," Taylor added.

‌



"There is already a great deal of talent and commitment within Turkey, and I look forward to working with colleagues across the Federation to build on those foundations and support the continued development of referees at every stage of the elite pathway.

View 2 Images Anthony Taylor will bring his expertise to Turkey (Image: Michael Regan/Getty Images)

"Retiring from elite refereeing was a significant decision, but I was always clear that I wanted to remain closely involved in the game and contribute to the future of officiating. This is an exciting opportunity to begin that next chapter, and I look forward to getting started."

‌



Taylor, from Altrincham, worked as a prison guard before becoming a professional referee. The 47-year-old suggested when announcing his retirement that the 'intense' pressure and 'constant' scrutiny had played a role in his decision.

In May 2023, Taylor and his family were harassed by Roma supporters at Budapest Airport following their Europa League final defeat to Sevilla and criticism from then-Roma manager Jose Mourinho. Taylor revealed last year that his family no longer came to watch matches that he refereed.

Sports.title: Xabi Alonso's task at Chelsea: 46-player squad, baffling transfers and confusing hierarchy
Sports.content:
Xabi Alonso knew perfectly well what he was signing himself up for when he agreed to become the next Chelsea manager.

"I had a view of Chelsea from the outside," Alonso told reporters while on Chelsea's pre-season tour of Australia. "I could see the positives and my concerns so I addressed them.

"We had the same ideas, the same analysis, to start building momentum together. That is why we are taking these steps together and making decisions to build a good team."

We don't need to ask Alonso what view he had of Chelsea before he arrived, because the picture has been painted very clearly over the past few years. It is one defined by muddied thinking and a chaotic approach, which comes together to create the biggest circus in the Premier League.

‌



Alonso is only in the early stages of his Chelsea career and will obviously need time to stamp his authority on things and turn around a side which finished a lowly 10th in the Premier League last season. Yet, despite having the title of manager, rather than head coach, he will have to do so within the same parameters of his predecessors Enzo Maresca and Liam Rosenior.

FOLLOW OUR CHELSEA FB PAGE! Latest Blues news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Chelsea sanctions reveal same punishment for sexual misconduct and ticket transferring READ MORE :

In the post-Roman Abramovich era, of which Todd Boehly has become the gormless face, Chelsea have become the most puzzling of entities where more confusion and baffling mismanagement is only around the corner. After all, this is a club that, defying convention, have five sporting directors.

It is a club, that at the time of writing, have 46 first-team players listed on their website. A club who have, despite their vast swathes of players, spent approximately £336million in the summer transfer window so far, with more no doubt to come.

‌



And a club which has, partly on Alonso's say-so, changed their youth-first transfer approach to sign 35-year-old Danny Welbeck and 36-year-old Jordan Henderson.

View 4 Images Jordan Henderson has joined Chelsea (Image: Chris Lee/Chelsea FC)

Welbeck's arrival means Chelsea currently have six senior strikers. Of them only Joao Pedro is assured of his position. Liam Delap, a £30m signing last summer, could be shipped out, Nicolas Jackson is looking for a new team after spending last season on loan at Bayern Munich and Marc Guiu is on the transfer list having been recalled from Sunderland last season due to injuries.

It is a muddled picture entirely in-keeping with Chelsea's modus operandi. Last summer, Maresca felt he had no other choice than to create a 'bomb squad', featuring the highly-paid group of Raheem Sterling, Axel Disasi, Joao Felix and Ben Chilwell.

‌



This summer it is Alonso who has the unenviable task of trying to work out which players he wants, which ones he doesn't and how to create some kind of squad unity amidst it all. Marc Cucurella may be gone after his frank criticism of the hierarchy, but senior players Enzo Fernandez and Moises Caicedo - who both publicly flirted with rival clubs during the slide under Rosenior - remain.

View 4 Images Xabi Alonso has a tough task creating unity in such a fragmented squad (Image: Darren Walsh/Chelsea FC via Getty Images)

"You need the right balance of personalities and stages of maturity, with players in their early 20s, early 30s and everything in between," Alonso has said of his squad. Yet the list of new arrivals shows the complicated squad picture the Spaniard has inherited from owners BlueCo:

Geovany Quenda (Sporting CP, undisclosed), Denner (Corinthians, undisclosed), Dastan Satpaev (Kairat Almaty, undisclosed), Emmanuel Emegha (Strasbourg, undisclosed), Marco Palestra (Atalanta, £47m), Morgan Rogers (Aston Villa, £117m), Maxence Lacroix (Crystal Palace, £52m), Danny Welbeck (Brighton, £5m), Jordan Henderson (Brentford, free), Valentin Barco (Strasbourg, undisclosed).

‌



Good luck getting your head around that, Xabi. Oh, and your ranks have been swelled even further by the return from a doping ban of Mykhailo Mudryk, the Ukrainian winger who has not played competitive football since November 2024.

View 4 Images Mykhailo Mudryk has returned to bolster ranks that didn't need bolstering (Image: May JAMES / AFP via Getty Images)

Keeping everyone happy will be an impossible balancing act, given the lack of European football means fewer matches. Perhaps more so than any other elite club, Chelsea is a dog-eat-dog environment where team spirit has been sorely missing in recent years.

Off the pitch there are more factors to try and get your head around. The £10m fine a suspended ban from registering new players for two transfer windows for historic off-the-books agent payments. The fact they are still yet to find a front-of-shirt sponsor, continuing their baffling commercial failure which stretches back to 2023.

‌



Yet, this being the ultimate club of contrasts, they have still splashed out six figures on a top-of-the-range private jet to whisk their players around during pre-season.

Chelsea have 20 days until their begin their Premier League campaign. The size of the task facing Alonso is such that it would be surprising if the picture appeared any clearer by then.

Sports.content:
Virgil van Dijk transfer lined up as club chiefs 'gutted' at missed Liverpool opportunity

An unexpected club has reportedly been planning a move for Liverpool's Virgil van Dijk

View 2 Images Virgil van Dijk is being eyed by an MLS club (Image: DeFodi Images, DeFodi Images via Getty Images)

Chicago Fire chiefs were said to be bitterly disappointed by Virgil van Dijk's absence from Liverpool's pre-season tour of America. The MLS club are reportedly lining up a transfer for the defender next summer and were keen to sell themselves to the Reds defender.

‌



The third and final stop of Liverpool's US tour this summer saw them face Leeds United in Chicago, Illinois, where they lost 4-2 on Sunday. Andoni Iraola's side played the match at Soldier Field, the home ground of Chicago Fire, having also used the MLS outfit's performance centre for training sessions.

‌



However, club captain Van Dijk was a notable absentee throughout the entire trip to the States. This was due to Liverpool granting him an extended summer break following his involvement with the Netherlands at the World Cup, meaning he was excused from joining the rest of the squad on tour.

‌



Yet, the 35-year-old's non-appearance is said to have left Chicago Fire staff "gutted". The Mail reports that the Fire have identified Van Dijk as a potential future acquisition.

The MLS club had been hoping to make an unofficial approach to the Dutchman by showcasing their world-class facilities, which were also utilised by Germany during the World Cup.

Sports.title: World Cup bombshell as ex-champs 'avoided anti-doping tests' for whole year before winning
Sports.content:
World Cup bombshell as ex-champs 'avoided anti-doping tests' for whole year before winning

Doubt has now emerged on the legitimacy of one World Cup title after shocking claims have emerged

View 2 Images France won their first World Cup title in 1998 (Image: Popperfoto via Getty Images)

The France national team were allegedly exempt from unannounced anti-doping tests for an entire year before winning the World Cup in 1998. That is according to Marie-George Buffet, who served as minister of sports under former Prime Minister Lionel Jospin from 1997 to 2002.

‌



Her revelations have come 13 years after denying such claims in front of a Senate Committee. The politician made the new statement during the documentary 'Zidane: The Making of a Legend', which focuses on the newly-appointed national team boss and his legendary playing career.

‌



However, it was overshadowed by Buffet's admission, which she said was sparked by a surprise anti-doping test during a training camp in Tignes in 1997. The tests were slammed by the players, then-manager Aime Jacquet and the French Football Federation (FFF), who accused the ministry of disrupting their preparations.

‌



All the urine tests had come back negative, but the furious reaction led Buffet to tell Alan Garnier - the doctor who carried out the tests - to no longer bother the team with anti-doping tests, according to Garnier himself.

According to Le Parisien, he said: "I was no longer to bother the French team until the World Cup. In short, no more unannounced tests." The doctor claimed the "verbal directive" was confirmed by Buffet, who acknowledged she faced pressures "of all kinds" when it came to leaving the national team alone.

Sports.title: 'Brutal, searing and punishing heat' - Babb on playing for Ireland at USA '94
Sports.content:
While none of the home nations qualified for the 1994 World Cup, the Republic of Ireland did.

It was a second successive appearance at the tournament for the Boys in Green, who were again led by 1966 World Cup winner Jack Charlton.

At Italia '90, the weather had been hot - but at USA '94, it was a different kettle of fish altogether.

The iconic image of Charlton launching an open bottle of water in the direction of Andy Townsend and Tommy Coyne always provides a reminder of that.

Image: Jack Charlton led the Republic of Ireland at Italia '90 and USA '94

He clashed with FIFA over their policy that bottles could not be thrown to the players on the pitch, so took to throwing the contents instead before FIFA later relented and allowed water bags to be thrown.

"They trust me to do what is right for them and I will continue to do it," Charlton said. "We have been right in pursuing this matter and FIFA's change of heart proves that."

Charlton was rarely seen without his white baseball cap that summer. Steve Staunton famously even wore one during the national anthem before the second group game against Mexico.

One of the players in the Ireland squad that summer was Phil Babb. The defender, then 23, had just completed his second full Premier League season at Coventry.

He made his international debut in a 0-0 friendly draw with Russia in March 1994, then played in the next four friendlies leading up to the tournament.

Image: Phil Babb played in all four of the Republic of Ireland's games at the 1994 World Cup

Nothing was set in stone, but he knew he would at least have a decent chance of being included in Charlton's 22-man squad, so started to physically prepare himself.

"A coach at Coventry asked me if I wanted to do anything specific - we ended up doing 12-minute sessions in a sauna!" Babb recalls, with a smile.

"We were doing burpees, press-ups, just trying to acclimatise to that intense heat. We did about six sessions - but I wouldn't recommend it for anyone now!

"I was a fit lad and had played pretty much all the Premier League games Coventry had played that season. I adapted to the heat pretty well, but I know some of the older lads really struggled."

Babb started alongside Paul McGrath in the heart of defence for Ireland's tournament opener at Giants Stadium in New Jersey.

Image: Ray Houghton's stunning strike earned a shock 1-0 win over Italy

That Saturday, they shocked an Italy side that featured Paolo Maldini, Franco Baresi and Roberto Baggio. John Aldridge's stunner sealed a memorable 1-0 win.

It was an achievement made all the more impressive by the fact the Azzurri went on to finish as runners-up - but also given the fact it was played in temperatures exceeding 30C.

"When we walked out onto the field, about two hours before kick-off, you could tell it was going to be absolutely roasting," he recalls.

"You could tell that straight away and we didn't stay out long. I just checked the grass to see which studs I wanted, then I went straight back in. I know some of the lads were walking around and taking the atmosphere in, but I thought: 'This is too hot'.

"I didn't go out for a warm-up with the rest of the lads, either. I stayed in the changing room. It was built for NFL, so they had a 40m sprint track. I warmed up in there and waited until we went out. It was brutal, it was searing, it was punishing.

"It affected everyone's game. You were saturated after just 10 minutes walking onto a pitch, so you had to conserve energy at the right times.

"Recovery was very basic and there was very little ball work because of the demands of the actual games and the fluids you lose. When you're that dehydrated, it's quite difficult. You want a drink, but you don't feel hungry and that is a key part of the recuperation."

Image: Babb, whose Ireland were knocked out by Dennis Bergkamp's Netherlands, joined Liverpool later that summer

Thirty-two years on from that tournament, football has evolved exponentially.

Sports science has taken on a key role in the game and, this summer, is likely to play into the way teams approach games tactically due to the heat. A slower tempo is expected in many.

Charlton was not prepared to facilitate the same in 1994, though.

"We only played one way, so if you tried to go off-piste, Jack would certainly let you know!" adds Babb.

"We had one style of play, with a lone striker. If it wasn't Tommy Coyne, it might have been Niall Quinn up there and we'd be putting long balls up to him, with either willing runners out wide or the midfield bombing on.

"That was the Irish way back then. Tommy ran tirelessly, to the point where he actually collapsed with heat exhaustion on the plane home.

"I think Jack's sports science was a barrel of Guinness in his room and he'd call the lads in and have a pint! I'm sure there's a high calorific content in that, so maybe he was ahead of his time!"

In spite of that, Babb's memories of the tournament are largely positive.

"I enjoyed it, I have to admit! I'd rather play in the searing heat than a wet Tuesday night in Hull," he says.

"I was a fit lad and it was quite easy for me playing alongside Paul McGrath, who was imperious in that tournament. I learned a lot from him and how he conserved his energy.

"I felt I got stronger because I got used to it. I guess our 0-0 draw against Norway would probably attest to the heat and the style of play.

"It all comes down to the individual. Footballers are supreme athletes now and they leave nothing to chance, so I think they'll cope a lot better than we did in the mid-90s."

The methods may have moved on since Charlton was throwing water onto the pitch, but Babb's memories from USA '94 provide a reminder this World Cup will be a battle against more than just the opposition.

Sports.title: Ogbene earns Republic of Ireland draw with Canada
Sports.content:
Chiedozie Ogbene's equaliser ensured the Republic of Ireland continued their good run of results as they drew 1-1 with World Cup co-hosts Canada in Montreal.

Canada went ahead in the 24th minute from an own goal by defender Jake O'Brien, heading a failed clearance into his own net from Stephen Eustaquio's corner.

Ireland were then awarded a penalty in the second half after Cyle Larin - who signed a two-year deal with Southampton earlier in the day - took out Jamie McGrath.

Canada goalkeeper Maxime Crepeau saved Troy Parrott's initial attempt, but Ogbene was on hand to slam home the rebound and tie the game in the 60th minute.

Image: Ireland's Jake O'Brien heads the ball into his own net

Ireland, who failed to qualify for this summer's World Cup, went close to a winner but Crepeau denied a charging run from Mason Melia late on.

The Orlando City goalkeeper missed out on the 2022 World Cup in Qatar after breaking his leg while playing in the MLS Cup final.

Canada, managed by former Leeds boss Jesse Marsch, officially open the World Cup on June 12 in Toronto against Bosnia and Herzegovina, before facing Qatar on June 18 and Switzerland on June 24.

They remain without captain Alphonso Davies, who is still nursing a hamstring injury he sustained while playing for Bayern Munich.

Sports.title: Republic of Ireland edge past Qatar in friendly as both sides end with 10
Sports.content:
Captain Nathan Collins headed the Republic of Ireland to a 1-0 friendly victory over World Cup-bound Qatar as both sides were reduced to 10 men.

Collins ensured Ireland got the better of a side managed by his former Wolves boss Julen Lopetegui with an early header.

However, just how the evening might have panned out had Jack Moylan not been dismissed as half-time approached, a sparse crowd inside the Aviva Stadium will never know.

Heimir Hallgrimsson's side, whose hopes of making it to the World Cup finals were dashed in heartbreaking fashion in March when they lost their play-off semi-final to the Czech Republic on penalties, were in complete control until Moylan's premature exit.

Qatar substitute Almoez Ali suffered the same fate 12 minutes from time.

Image: Jack Moylan was sent off before half-time at the Aviva Stadium

The game was played out against the backdrop of ongoing unease at the forthcoming Nations League clashes with Israel, and play was interrupted on several occasions during the first half as 'Stop the Game' protesters among a crowd of 28,981 repeatedly hurled tennis balls on to the pitch.

Ireland will now head for Montreal and their friendly against World Cup co-hosts Canada on June 6, while Qatar continue their preparations for the finals - they launch their Group B campaign against Switzerland in San Francisco on June 13 - against El Salvador in Los Angeles on the same day.

The Republic took the lead with just five minutes gone when, having been fouled by Ayoub Al-Oui wide on the left, Moylan curled the resulting free-kick on to the head of Collins, who glanced the ball effortlessly past 'keeper Mahmoud Abunada.

Image: Qatar's Almoez Ali was also sent off

There was a brief interruption after the protesters made their presence felt for the first time as Qatar's Pedro Miguel underwent treatment for injury, but once order had been restored, Troy Parrott whipped a first-time shot wide after being picked out by Seamus Coleman.

The Qataris simply could not get anywhere near Hallgrimsson's men and a mid-half drinks break did little to improve matters for the visitors with Abunada having to field Jayson Molumby's deflected 24th-minute shot from distance.

Lopetegui could not hide his frustration on the sideline and only the bravery of defender Ahmed Fathi denied Chiedozie Ogbene a second goal as he attempted to latch on to Liam Scales' header back across goal.

But the home side's night took a turn for the worse on the stroke of half-time when Northern Irish referee Jamie Robinson deemed Moylan's challenge on Jassem Gaber worthy of a red card, much to the Lincoln frontman's clear astonishment.

Image: Former Wolves and West Ham boss Julen Lopetegui is now in charge of Qatar

With defender James Abankwah having replaced Dara O'Shea at half-time, the 10 men found themselves under pressure for the first time on their return, although Coleman very nearly caught Abunada off his line with an audacious 52nd-minute attempt from the right wing.

Edmilson Junior dragged a long-range effort wide two minutes later after Molumby went down in midfield under Fathi's challenge and it took a fine 71st-minute reaction save by Caoimhin Kelleher - his first of the night - to keep out Yusuf Abdurisag's deflected shot.

However, Qatari hopes of salvation were dashed with 12 minutes remaining when Ali struck out at Molumby off the ball on several occasions and was also sent off.

Sports.title: Parrott out of luck as Republic of Ireland draw with North Macedonia
Sports.content:
Troy Parrott had two goals disallowed as the Republic of Ireland played out a stalemate against North Macedonia on the night on which they had hoped to book a trip to the World Cup finals.

Five days after their dreams came to an end for another four years in Prague, Ireland drew 0-0 with the Macedonians in a friendly encounter neither side wanted as the Czech Republic and Denmark fought for the big prize.

Even a third successive home victory for the first time since the 2015-16 campaign would have provided scant consolation for Thursday night's disappointment but Heimir Hallgrimsson's men had to make do with a disappointing draw.

AZ Alkmaar striker Parrott came closest to breaking the deadlock as 37-year-old defender Seamus Coleman received a standing ovation from a crowd of 39,560 at the Aviva Stadium when he was replaced during the second half of what could yet prove to be his final appearance for his country.

Nevertheless, the squad will reconvene for a series of friendlies at the end of the season ahead of next season's Nations League campaign and later Euro 2028 qualification having restored a measure of pride and established a momentum they hope will serve them well when they return to competitive action.

The hosts went on to the offensive from the off, although they were unable to find the final ball to allow either Parrott or Chiedozie Ogbene to threaten.

John Egan could not direct an 11th-minute corner at goal and Ogbene saw his snapshot deflected over three minutes later, but goalkeeper Caoimhin Kelleher had to parry Enis Bardhi's 21st-minute free-kick after it flicked off the defensive wall, with Bardhi volleying high over after the resulting corner had been only half-cleared.

Macedonia keeper Stole Dimitrievski saved Parrott's 23rd-minute header comfortably after Dara O'Shea and Finn Azaz had sparked a concerted attack, and Azaz failed to make the most of a free-kick two minutes later after he had been tripped just outside the penalty area.

Parrott was played into a promising position by Knight nine minutes before the break, only to miss the target by some distance.

The in-form striker - he scored his sixth goal in three games in Prague - might have done better again two minutes later after Azaz's clipped pass had caused problems for the Macedonian defence but he snatched at his attempt and fired high and wide.

Parrott twice had the ball in the net as time ran down but an offside flag stalled his celebrations on each occasion.

Ireland were unfortunate not to take the lead with 52 minutes gone when Azaz accepted Seamus Coleman's pass and found Parrott, who turned smartly before shooting against the upright.

Azaz curled an effort just wide and Tihomir Kostadinov denied Parrott a clear run on goal as the hosts began to turn the screw but it was veteran Coleman's 61st-minute departure as

Hallgrimsson made changes which attracted the biggest cheer of the night to that point.

Wholesale changes did not help the flow of the game, which rather petered out as the whistle approached, although Ireland substitute Johnny Kenny passed up a glorious opportunity to win it at the end with a weak shot at the keeper.

Sports.title: Szmodics out of hospital and 'on the mend' after collision
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland forward Sammie Szmodics has been released from hospital in Prague after being knocked unconscious during Thursday's World Cup play-off defeat by the Czech Republic.

The 24-year-old, who is currently on loan at Derby from Ipswich, was hurt in a collision with defender Stepan Chaloupek just two minutes after his introduction as an extra-time substitute at the Fortuna Arena, sparking concerned medics to rush to his aid.

Szmodics was carried from the field on a stretcher and taken straight to hospital, where Ireland head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson later revealed he would spend the night under observation.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Danyal Khan looks back on the heartbreaking result for the Republic of Ireland who lost their World Cup qualifying play-off against Czech Republic on penalties

A Football Association of Ireland spokesperson said on Friday morning: "Sammie Szmodics was transferred to hospital yesterday having sustained a head injury during extra time of the play-off against Czechia.

"Following further tests and a period of observation, he has been safely discharged from hospital and will continue his recovery under the care of the Republic of Ireland and Derby County medical teams."

Szmodics, who Hallgrimsson confirmed would have taken a penalty in the shoot-out which Ireland ultimately lost 4-3, took to social media to express his thanks to those who had helped him.

He posted on X: "Gutted the way it ended. Fans and boys immense all evening!! Appreciate everyone's messages. And thank you to the medical staff who acted so quickly to help me. On the mend."
